docs.title: FontLab Scriptmix
docs.text:
Scriptmix contains small scripts for FontLab's Scripts menu. Use the reports to inspect an open font. Use the editors to preview a change before you apply it. Canvas reporters draw on the Glyph window without changing the font.

Start with installation. The script catalogue contains the purpose, full usage description, source hash and immutable source link for every current menu script.

The working with scripts page explains font selection, previews and window cleanup. The documentation guide explains how to rebuild this site from the checked-out source.

docs.title: Catalogue and acceptance scope
docs.text: The practical catalogue contains all 261 current menus. The broader classified offline smoke covers 350 scripts; that classification is separate from native acceptance. The original native denominator remains 130, with only the historically qualified 68 smokes retained. New documentation renews none of those native results. Read the full porting backlog, historical integration guide and Text Holder guide.

docs.title: Clear Backgrounds Across a Font
docs.text:
Open Cleanup > Clear All Layer Backgrounds to scan every glyph and every physical foreground layer in the current font. Clear Master Backgrounds includes only declared master layers, including non-interpolating masters. Auxiliary layers with interpolatable names are not treated as declared masters.

The table follows original glyph and layer order. Clear backgrounds removes the entire original background object, including outlines, anchors, guidelines, images and stored properties. It does not rebuild a partial copy or clear only contours. Refresh rereads the original font. Closing the window cancels future actions; it cannot reverse an already applied edit.

One native mask can be shared by several foreground layers. The all-layer tool removes it once. The master-only tool refuses a mask shared with an excluded auxiliary layer. Unmapped masks and ambiguous identities refuse before history; no layer is silently omitted. Automatic layers/dependants and pending native updates also prevent writing because their complete history preservation has not been qualified. Switching fonts invalidates the original tool.

An unchanged scan performs no history or date writes. A successful edit uses one final native notification. If a native operation fails after removal begins, the tool reports an explicit partial outcome and recommends Edit > Undo. It never reconstructs deleted backgrounds or claims an exception rolled back.

These are independent Python 3.11 FontLab implementations of Pedro Arilla's Apache-2.0 scripts Clear background in all layers.py and Clear background in all master layers.py from pedroarilla/glyphs-scripts, with shared logic available through fly.ap.masters.background.clear.model. The originals remain in the source corpus, unchanged. See NOTICE for attribution.

docs.title: Qualification
docs.text: Source and ordinary installed-artifact controls are separate from FontLab acceptance. The complete native whole-font background mapping, survivor metadata, one Undo/Redo, dirty state, timestamps and save/reopen workflow remain pending owned-font qualification. Native limitations are not completion of the original workflow. Existing source-migration denominators remain unchanged.

docs.title: Active and Locked Background Boundary
docs.text:
An active background cannot be removed while preserving that active layer. The tool refuses it before history. Locked backgrounds also refuse: the bound read-only resolver does not reveal whether the stored active pointer is locked. These cases remain part of the original required workflow and are not accepted through refusal. The complete original target list remains in the preview.

The scan uses updateActiveLayer(False), which does not assign a replacement. It never reads activeLayer or isActive, whose native getters can initialize a previously null active pointer. Null/unreadable resolution on a nonempty glyph refuses the scan. Final source and pending-update fences occur after all staged inputs, immediately before history preparation.

After any attempted removal, every pre/post date error is collected and exactly one final notification is attempted even if stamping fails. A notification failure remains an explicit partial outcome. No-op and no-attempt paths never notify or write dates. Expected survivor order is prepared in checked per-glyph passes before history, not a quadratic whole-font traversal after it.

docs.title: Porting backlog
docs.text:
The active menu contains 242 practical tools: 69 sample adaptations and 173 additional tools. Source and native acceptance differ; new reviewed candidates retain their pending native status in additional-tools.json and their docstrings.

These 61 archived launchers were removed from Scripts, not completed. Every original has a historical path/hash identity in the external archive described in NOTICE. rescue-index.json retains the historical menu path, source path and SHA-256. The other 69 sample originals also retain their historical identities. The sample migration denominator stays 130; released acceptance remains 68/130, with the Italic Angle candidate and these 61 ports still subject to their existing gates. The wider Glyphs source corpus, PythonQt adaptations, package cleanup and native acceptance remain in scope.

docs.text:
Source SHA-256 Destination Disposition mekkablue/Glyphs-Scripts/Smallcaps/Check Smallcap Consistency.py 515a006343efe90ea922f63da932e9298224de31e12226a4cb242ed91c814ab0 Reports/Smallcap Consistency.py Modern and legacy report source workflows implemented; native acceptance pending. Corrected counterpart Boolean; retained counts, export filtering, suffix/Unicode orphans, missing capital/lowercase and both kerning-group sides.

FontLab capture uses public.skipExportGlyphs as an explicitly labelled export policy and exact SC suffix particles for classification. Unknown name mappings and ambiguous groups remain visible. Legacy legacy_lowercase_without_smallcaps independently reports missing exporting .sc glyphs even when modern .smcp coverage passes. Native timing, complete-font preservation, installed origins, repeat refresh and report destruction still need owned-font qualification. Synchronous getters cannot be preempted; budget checks on return refuse partial output. This one port does not complete the wider corpus.

No native/full-port or automatic MRU-equivalence claim.

All four defaults and option persistence are preserved. Multiple encodings are alternatives; expansions retain complete strings. Preferred names precede encoded aliases; ambiguities, math, ligatures and unknowns remain visible. The public.skipExportGlyphs export policy is compatibility-only. Inactive ambiguous FontLab views require explicit selection because hidden Glyphs remembered-current ordering has no equivalent exposed binding.

docs.title: Build and edit the documentation
docs.text:
The source configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. Authored pages are in src_docs/md. The build writes the static site to docs.

./build.sh
./build.sh --offline
./build.sh --serve

The first build needs network access to install the packages pinned in src_docs/requirements.txt. Use --offline after those packages are cached. The build needs Python 3.12 or later and uv. It does not start FontLab or execute the scripts shown on a page.

Serve starts a local preview. Live Edit is available only in that preview; it saves changes to the authored Markdown. The static site has no editing server. Edit generated catalogue pages through their source generator, because the next build replaces them.

docs.title: Include source and shared text
docs.text: Keep usage and setup in the script docstring. The generator publishes descriptions, exact hashes and immutable source links; it keeps implementation snapshots outside the public site. Use mkdocstrings with Python inspection disabled when documenting an importable module. Menu scripts and archived host scripts are displayed as source instead.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
Name the action and its scope. Give one instruction per step where possible. Put prerequisites before the action. Keep exact API identifiers and interface labels. State a host limitation beside the operation that it affects. This is ASD-STE100-inspired writing; it is not a claim of controlled-language certification.

Use page tags and categories to connect related tasks. The navigation follows .nav.yml. Use the print page for a combined printable copy.

docs.title: Build function reference
docs.text:
This section documents the source-only build helper for contributors.

The generator reads source files and recorded hashes without importing menu scripts.

docs.title: Complete cross-font reports
docs.text:
Make the intended reference font current. The composite report needs another font; the glyph-set report preserves the original successful empty output when no other font is open. Report Composite Differences compares only the first other open font, with each font's selected named master. Component base names stay in their stored order, including repetitions. Different common glyphs use name;source bases;target bases; rows. Missing glyphs stay in reference order; only case-sensitive .sc and .pcap endings are excluded.

Report Glyph Set Differences compares every other open font in open-font order. Each raw filepath heading is followed by target-order Extra rows, then reference-order Missing rows. An unsaved empty native filepath maps to the original None heading. No chooser changes the reference or target policy.

Both reports are nonmodal, read-only and selectable. Refresh repeats the complete original scan and diagnoses changed sources. No font, selection, history, preferences or user Output is changed. Report text can contain source filepaths because that is an explicit original result, but packages/docs contain no local source paths. Literal copying is preserved by the shared editor; actual PythonQt literal-NUL and complete-font getter preservation remain native gates. Unknown selected-master mappings are diagnosed without activation or fallback; full original master domains remain required for native acceptance.

Originals by Jens Kutilek, MIT; full notice is in NOTICE. Source bodies/resources remain untouched and unexecuted. These are new workflows, not entries counted as completed in the historical130sample ledger.

docs.title: Install the scripts
docs.text:
These scripts use FontLab 9's Python 3.11 and its PythonQt binding. Install fontlab-fly and a matching fontlab-fontlabapp>=1.2.0 artifact in FontLab's Python environment. Feature editors also need App's fontedit extra and native fontpr. TMetrics Window requires a FontLabApp build providing fontlabapp.fontui.tmetrics; TGlyph Window requires fontlabapp.fontui.tglyph. Both also need App's fontport extra. These two windows have no verified numeric release floor. The documentation build uses a separate Python environment.

  1. Open FontLab's Scripts folder.
  2. Copy the contents of this repository's Scripts folder into that folder.
  3. Keep the category folders. FontLab supports one folder level in the Scripts menu.
  4. Open a font. Choose a script from the corresponding category in the Scripts menu.

Start with Reports > Font Overview to inspect the font. Read the script's description before you run an editor. Test edits on a copy of the font.

Close a script's panel with its Close control. The shared lifecycle code disconnects the script's signals and destroys its owned window.

docs.title: Close But No Cigar
docs.text:
Select glyphs in a Font or Glyph window, then choose Scripts → Reports → Close But No Cigar. The modeless report has selectable text, Refresh, and Close. It reports suspicions; it does not move nodes or change stem values. It preserves the Output panel.

The complete menu source delegates lazily through fly.ap.contours.near_miss.model to App 1.2.0 or later. Native FontLab qualification remains pending. Python 3.11 source, ordinary archive installations, independent original-contract controls and standalone Qt checks are separate evidence.

docs.title: Selection and master scope
docs.text:
Every selected occurrence is processed in order, including repeated parents. Each parent contributes its literal first layer, even when another layer is selected or active. No current-glyph fallback is used. The report resolves that layer's associated named font master and reads that master's PostScript horizontal/vertical stems, ascender, cap height, x height and descender. It never substitutes the active master's data or calls a master/selection writer.

FontLab associates a named layer by the part before :, # or @, as in its FontMetrics source. The report requires that name to match exactly one serialized master. Unknown or ambiguous associations refuse the whole report, rather than using FontLab's implicit key-master fallback. Components are omitted, matching the original own-path scope. Own affine element transforms map nodes into layer coordinates.

docs.title: Complete original checks
docs.text:
For every own path, segment checks precede node checks, preserving original order:

  • Angles strictly within two degrees of 0, 180, 90 or -90 are reported, except exact values. The original asymmetric treatment of negative 180 degrees is retained; no angle normalization is added.
  • Horizontal-direction segments near 0/180 compare against every horizontal stem. Vertical-direction segments near ±90 compare against every vertical stem. A length must be strictly between 95% and 105% of a target, and unequal to it. An exact length match to any stem suppresses every near-stem message for that orientation. Duplicate stem targets retain duplicate messages.
  • Every node, including off-curve handles, receives six position checks: x near zero; y near zero, ascender, cap height, x height and descender. Each test is strictly within two units and excludes exact values. Equal metric targets retain their separate labelled messages.

Line length is the endpoint distance; angle is the endpoint atan2 in degrees. Cubic length retains glyphmonkey's 50-step repeated t += 0.02 sampling, including its last sample below 1.0 and exact floating-point arithmetic association. That matters because exact-stem suppression is part of the contract. It is not an analytic curve length.

docs.title: Explicit source repairs and refusals
docs.text:
Simon Cozens' helper overrides a cubic's inherited angle property with an undecorated method. The original script reads it as a number and can fail on curves. This adaptation repairs that mismatch using the helper's intended endpoint angle. Empty contours safely contribute no segment. The helper's last-to-first starting edge is retained even on open contours; the closing-edge suspicion therefore remains visible.

TrueType contours with off-curve controls and malformed non-line/non-cubic runs refuse the complete report. Two quadratic controls must never be interpreted as cubic handles. Generated shapes, projective transforms, unreadable numbers, missing first layers, unknown master association, stale source changes and expired scans also refuse the complete report. No report prefix survives a failed Refresh; restore the source and Refresh again.

docs.title: Raise Ascender
docs.text:
Choose Contours > Raise Ascender in Scriptmix (App .157 or later). Enter an Amount (default 10). Raise this master, the default action, processes every currently selected layer occurrence in selection order. Repeated occurrences remain repeated. Raise all masters processes every foreground layer of the first selected glyph, including auxiliary/service layers; its historical label does not mean master layers only. Both actions leave the window and Amount open.

Every own path node, including off-curve controls and quadratic nodes, moves by Amount when its current layer-space y is strictly greater than xHeight + 10 for that layer's associated master. Components remain unchanged. A repeated negative move can cross the threshold, so the next occurrence then does nothing. Each changed occurrence creates a separate native Undo notification. No-op occurrences do not manufacture history. The original overlapping controls have been laid out separately; action names, default and input remain intact.

The original source is Simon Cozens' MIT GlyphsScripts/Raise Ascender.py. The original loop and all target domains remain the contract. The FontLab writer stages detached shapes, restores raw node flags/names and ShapeData notes after native cloning, and keeps all untouched components/shapes attached. The complete action is preflighted before the first history operation. Changes to font, selection, metrics or geometry stop later occurrences. Failures are diagnosed, notification is attempted after an attempted mutation, and no global Undo or UpdateAll is invoked. Inspect any retained partial changes with Edit > Undo. This balanced failure handling intentionally repairs the original swallowed, potentially unbalanced Undo errors.

Native qualification is pending. Exact named masters and unambiguous imported masterName.auxName associations are supported in source; an arbitrary auxiliary association or implicit editor slot is not guessed from the active master. Generated/nested geometry, locked layers, hinted shape replacement, automatic layers/dependants and pending native update queues have explicit whole-action refusals. These remain incomplete original domains, not completed by refusal. Finite input/results are required for native safety; NaN/infinity are never silently normalized. Metadata, history/Redo and full saved/reopened font preservation still require owned FontLab qualification. No font selection, master, live installation, preferences or clipboard is changed by opening UI.

Retained callbacks are inert after normal Close or parent destruction. A failed Close keeps the live error diagnosis available while cleanup can be retried.

docs.title: Installation and Reports
docs.text:
Copy the contents of Scripts into your FontLab Scripts menu folder. Keep the category subfolders, such as Reports and Font Info; FontLab supports one folder level. Use FontLab 9's Python 3.11 with fontlab-fly and fontlab-fontlabapp (including scripting) available in its Python environment. No third-party UI package is needed.

Open a font, then run Empty Glyphs, Open Contours or Font Overview from Reports. The dialogs are modeless: edit the font and Rescan/Refresh when needed. Empty Glyphs can hide intentional whitespace. Select chosen rows, or leave rows unselected to select all results. Selection refuses results after changing the current font; rescan first. Reports read all masters without changing geometry. Closing a report disconnects its signals. Re-running replaces its old window. Close also destroys the native dialog after its event finishes. All eight reports share this lifecycle code through fly.ap.core.scripting.

Sources stay archived until full reconciliation; migration.json records exact Apache-2.0 provenance/hashes and WORK.md retains native acceptance receipts.

A failed scan or table refresh invalidates selection until a complete rescan succeeds. Partial results are cleared; explicit selection calls also refuse them.

docs.title: Reports: second migration batch
docs.text:
Live Glyph Info follows the selected glyph twice a second, with per-master metrics, outline/component/anchor counts and Pause. Glyph Table CSV offers all or selected glyphs, sortable widths/counts, Copy CSV and a modeless UTF-8 CSV save chooser. Label Statistics shows mark colours and suffix groups; Add to selection preserves the current selection. Nodes Near Zones checks transformed on-curve nodes across masters with selection scope and a 1–30 unit tolerance. Unicode Coverage includes untouched-block filtering, progress bars and block selection. Explicit selection is bound to the font that supplied the rows.

All five retain the original interactions and pass their original native scenarios, including the live timer and owned Close, on FontLab9.0.9784.

docs.title: Font Info tools
docs.text:
The Font Info menu includes Glyph Order Preview and Export, Master Metrics Table, Names and Credits, Unicode Ranges and Codepages, Bump Font Version and Calculate Vertical Metrics. All original controls, embedded Unicode data, assessment notices, export, previews and the metric diagram are retained.

Names changes style on the original current master and credits font-wide. Master Metrics edits every displayed master. Version bump optionally appends a dated note to every master. Vertical Metrics defaults to hhea and Win; Typo is optional because it also moves FontLab's own ascender/descender lines. Its bounds are captured on open; reopen after outline changes. Glyph Order exports UTF-8 text without reordering the font; Unicode coverage reports without editing it.

Apply uses the last complete preview, refuses closed/switched fonts and changed source values, validates the entire plan before writes, preserves the active master and rolls back attempted fields on failure. Failed previews disable Apply. Names and current-master vertical metrics also refuse a master switch. No-op plans add no history. The shared metadata helper notifies only the package and its master container. Fontport's existing history protocol may add an extra no-op Undo checkpoint. All six pass their original native scenarios on FontLab 9.0.9784. All four editors pass one-step Undo, Redo, saved metadata reopening and complete font-data preservation. Native tests also verify no-op history and switched-font refusal. Shared panels load lazily through Fontlabapp; each tool keeps its own controls and actions. Glyph Order uses an owned modeless save chooser and reports the exported count and filename.

docs.title: Feature tools
docs.text:
Features contains Alternate Preview, Build Suffix Substitution, Classes Browser, Feature Code Viewer, Ligature Finder and Suffix Report. They preserve the original master proof, filters, selection, literal search/highlights and Copy controls. Proof rows use one outline scale per master and wrap large families.

Build previews actual suffix substitutions and appends them to the requested feature, retaining prefix, ordered unrelated features and classes. Apply binds to the original font, complete feature source and referenced glyphs. It uses Fontport's existing ordered writer and Undo safety checks through App, skips no-ops and reports unexpected native failures as possibly partial. Install App's optional fontedit dependency for Build and Feature Code Viewer; native fontpr must be available. The viewer reads exact stored prefix/ordered blocks, rather than native iterator values or synthesized class-prefix text. It does not compile features: test the result in FontLab's Features panel.

These six tools pass their native scenarios and actual Close destruction. The builder passes complete feature-only saved deltas, one-step Undo, Redo and reopening. All20migrated tools pass183workflow checks together on FontLab9.0.9784. Clipboard operations remain host-free tested; native checks inspect the actual suffix preview under the owner's clipboard exclusion. No export chooser is needed: these six originals provide Copy, not file export.

docs.title: Host-free distribution checks
docs.text:
Run with Python 3.11 through uv and an explicit current App requirement: 

SCRIPTMIX_APP_REQUIREMENT=/path/to/current-app.whl ./test.sh
# Proof needs App0.2.10 helpers; build the current checkout:
uv build /path/to/app --out-dir /path/to/dist
SCRIPTMIX_APP_REQUIREMENT=/path/to/dist/current-app.whl ./test.sh

Cached uv requirements permit offline wheel tests. Sources resolve without native binaries; development may set SCRIPTMIX_APP_SOURCE=/path/to/app/src/fontlabapp alongside the explicit dependency. Missing helpers fail the run.

Every default run checks all 54 destination hashes, exact menu paths/depth, Python 3.11 syntax and provenance metadata. It does not audit absent originals. To additionally check every original source hash, provide the workspace root containing externally restored historical fontlab-python-examples paths (see the archive identities in NOTICE):

SCRIPTMIX_APP_REQUIREMENT=/path/to/current-app.whl ./test.sh --original-source-root /path/to/workspace

An absent external source folder skips only its optional byte audit. A present archive with missing files or mismatched hashes fails. Historical source hashes remain recorded; this guide describes the earlier release layout.

docs.text:

Oversized proof fits its complete ink, including accents and overhangs. No font data is written.

The two additional editors need App0.2.9 helpers from that same wheel/source recipe. Exceptions Finder lists broader class overrides, offers Tick redundant/Untick all and removes exactly ticked rows. docs.title: Text Holder
docs.text:
Open Utilities > Text Holder for an editable floating proof-text scratchpad. The initial editor content is500×400; decorated frame limits are500×400..1200×800. It needs no open font. Type or paste plain text. Find highlights the first case-sensitive literal match from the start, preserving text and the previous selection when no match exists. Find & Replace replaces every literal match inside the selected range; with no selection it replaces matches throughout the document. An empty Find field changes nothing. Empty replacement deletes matches. Unicode cursor ranges use Qt UTF16 units; emoji prefixes and non-BMP selections are handled explicitly.

Save writes the current text and keeps the editor open. Save & Close saves first and closes only after success. Ignore & Close, Escape and the window close button discard only unsaved edits. Reopen to recover the last saved text. The window size persists separately, including when text is ignored. Unsuccessful saving retains the draft and the previous saved file, with an error in the window. An unreadable saved text file refuses opening rather than presenting a blank editor that could silently overwrite it.

The default file is Text holder.txt in Qt application-specific data storage for FontLab, with a Text holder.window.json size sidecar. The directory is only created by an explicit Save or window-size save on Close. Tests and native qualification must pass an explicit owned temporary path to App show(path=...), or inject the default location into an owned directory. No validation uses the users saved text. Validation changes no global preferences, fonts, selection, history, Output or system clipboard. User-invoked Copy/Cut retain normal clipboard behavior. There is no autosave of draft content.

App1.2.0 and Fly are required. The menus and editor are independently implemented from Reza Bohlouls Window/Text holder.py; no licence declaration was found, and no original body is redistributed or executed. Apache2.0 terms for the new implementation remain in the repository licence files. Native FontLab/PythonQt lifecycle and storage acceptance remains pending.

The initial500×400 dimensions are content size. The original native window minimum500×400 and maximum1200×800 constrain the decorated frame; Qt client limits subtract the measured frame extents after first show. The window-size sidecar stores decorated frame dimensions and restoration subtracts those same logical extents, preserving the original frame-based autosave semantics.

The original explicitly sets Cocoa frame origin(0,500) after frame recovery. On first show the Qt position is(primary-screen.left, primary-screen.top + primary-screen.height −500−current decorated frame.height). This uses full logical screen geometry, with no available-area offset, DPR multiplication or clamping of negative top positions. Raising/hiding/showing an existing window retains its manually moved position; reopening reapplies the original placement. FontLab primaryScreen is a null property binding in the known host; the known safe QApplication.screens()[0] route supplies its primary screen geometry. Final native qualification must verify the current host screen ordering and actual decorated frame dimensions on the final combined artifact.

The window retains the original normal NSWindow role while floating above normal windows: Qt.Window with WindowStaysOnTopHint, title/system/close and minimize/maximize hints. It is not a Qt.Tool/NSPanel that hides on deactivation. Actual native minimization, app deactivation and reactivation remain part of the root-owned combined .100 qualification. No native result is claimed here.

Literal NBSP, Unicode line separator(U+2028) and paragraph separator(U+2029) remain distinct from space and ordinary LF during editing, Find, replacement, Save and recovery. Undo/Redo, typing, input-method commits and text paste/copy preserve these literal characters as well. As in the original Python open(...,'r'), disk loading translates CRLF and lone CR to LF; this is separate from preserving literal text authored in the editor.

docs.title: Add Anchors From File
docs.text:
Import named anchor coordinates from a UTF-8 CSV file.

What: Add or move named anchors on the current master for every CSV glyph row. How: Use name or glyph plus paired anchor_x,anchor_y columns. Strip header whitespace; refuse unknown columns, missing glyphs and malformed rows. Two empty coordinate cells leave that anchor unchanged. Coordinates round half up to font units before preview and writing. Report BOM and newline conversions only when they occur. Existing pins keep their appearance and expressions. Why: A checked table avoids repeated manual entry and preference-dependent fractional writes. Automatic layers are kept; unsafe writes are refused. Use: Browse for a CSV, click Load, inspect the non-modal preview, then Import. Benefit: Apply a complete coordinate table consistently. Each application is recorded as one Undo step.

Source: Simon Cozens, https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts, MIT, copyright 2017 Simon Cozens. Independent behaviour rewrite; no source code was copied.

Run Anchors > Add Anchors From File from FontLab's Scripts menu.

Read installation and working with scripts before use.

docs.text:
Fit missing entry and exit anchors to a saved cursive sample.

What: Fit missing connection pins for right-to-left scripts on the current master. Search exit from the left edge and entry from the right edge. How: Read a JSON sample from Get Sample. Require matching master names. Name fragments ini/med request exit; fin/med request entry. Keep existing pins. Score near-edge ink thickness and polygon-edge tangent estimates; a perfect zero score is valid. Use nonzero winding on closed decomposed outlines. Round half up to font units. Report actual text conversions. Why: A persistent sample gives a reusable attachment standard. Layer failures become note rows so clean selected glyphs can still run. Use: Select glyphs, Browse for the sample, inspect the preview, then Add. Benefit: Place consistent right-to-left cursive connections. Each application is recorded as one Undo step.

docs.title: Center Horizontally
docs.text:
Put named anchors on the horizontal centre of the advance or of the ink box.

What: Moves the named anchors sideways. A slider sets the target between the left edge (0 %) and the right edge (100 %) of the advance width or of the ink box. The y value never changes.

How: With an italic angle the target is a slanted line. For the advance it passes through the baseline point; for the ink box it passes through the centre of the box. So a top anchor of an italic glyph moves right as its height grows. FontLab angle convention: a negative angle leans right. Example: advance 500, centre, angle -10 degrees, y 700: x = 373.

Why: One rule for upright and italic glyphs. The panel starts with the font italic angle of the current master and lets you override it. Reload selection keeps your value. With all masters, one angle serves every master and the panel says so.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Type the anchor names. Choose advance or ink box. Move the slider. Check the table. Press Centre.

Benefit: Mark anchors sit on the optical centre in every master, in one step.

Safety: Auto layers are listed and never edited. The script refuses the whole batch, before any history exists, when:

  • an existing anchor would move to 0, 0 (FontLab cannot Redo that);
  • a glyph has an automatic layer, or is the base of an automatic composite, also through other composites (FontLab rebuilds the composite and Undo does not restore it);
  • several anchors on a layer share a name (the edit is ambiguous);

After the write, the script reads every value back. It reports any value that FontLab did not keep, for example under a strong rounding preference. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The edit is recorded as one Undo step. The plan, the safety checks, the one-step write and the panel base are shared with the other anchor scripts (fly.ap.anchors.writer, fly.ap.anchors.panel.model); the planner and the controls belong to this script.

Source: the author's own FontLab sample anchors_center_horizontally.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

Run Anchors > Center Horizontally from FontLab's Scripts menu.

Read installation and working with scripts before use.

docs.title: Cloud View
docs.text:
Overlay the selected glyphs faintly and show every anchor of one name as a cloud of dots, per master.

What it does: A tight cloud means marks will sit consistently; a stray dot is a glyph whose anchor is off. Hover-free and read-only: the list under each panel gives the extreme values. Nothing in the font is changed.

docs.title: Mirror Across Masters
docs.text:
Copy the anchors of one master into the other masters of the same glyphs.

What: Takes the anchors of a source master. Moves the same-named anchors in the ticked target masters, and adds the missing ones. Optional: add only the missing anchors.

How: The x value can scale with the advance-width ratio, target over source. An anchor in the middle of a narrow Light glyph then lands in the middle of the wide Bold glyph. Positions round half up to whole units. A new anchor gets its name-derived appearance.

Why: One master carries the reference design. The others follow in one step. This is a start: interpolation or hand work refines the result.

  • a glyph has an automatic layer, or is the base of an automatic composite, also through other composites (FontLab rebuilds the composite and Undo does not restore it);
  • several anchors on a layer share a name (the edit is ambiguous);

After the write, the script reads every value back. It reports any value that FontLab did not keep, for example under a strong rounding preference. docs.title: Optical Center
docs.text:

What: Move one third from the bounds centre toward the horizontal ink median. How: Flatten the placed layer path once, including components. Master layers, automatic, mask, service, image and temporary "|temp|" layers are never deleted on their own. The empty mask of a deleted layer is removed first, so no orphan mask stays. All deletions run in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. FontLab records the step only for layers plus their glyph, so the notification holds the first master layer of each glyph, which stays. Then the script checks by layer id that each deleted layer and mask is gone.

Why this design: - No dialog: the script deletes only layers that carry no data, and the deletion is recorded as one Undo step. A preview would show only names. - The shown (active) layer of a glyph is kept, so FontLab never has to pick another shown layer. A locked layer, or one with a locked mask, is kept: a lock is a deliberate "keep". - The deleted layers and masks hold no shapes, so no component has to be retained for Undo (fl#7641). - Glyphs with automatic layers and bases of automatic composites (also through manual composites) are skipped and named in the result. A notification there makes FontLab rebuild the automatic glyphs, and Undo does not restore them. - The run discloses queued ids and their possible date changes.

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window (Select All for the whole font), or open one glyph. Run the script. Read the result in the Output panel. Use "Layer Cleanup" to delete layers that hold data.

Benefit: Leftover empty layers from imports and experiments go in one key press.

docs.title: Align By Anchor
docs.text:
Align mark components on their base component by anchors.

What: In each selected composite, the first component is the base. Every later component (a mark) moves so that its "_name" anchor lands on the base's "name" anchor. The table shows the anchor pair, the current offset and the new offset per master.

How: New offset = base offset + base anchor - mark anchor, rounded half up to whole units. The anchors come from the base and mark glyphs on the same master. "Automatic" takes the first pair the two glyphs share; or choose one anchor name. Only the offset changes: the component itself stays in place in the layer, with its name, note and lock.

Why: Marks drift when anchors move after a composite was built. This puts them back without a rebuild, and keeps manual composites manual. Components with scale, slant or rotation are listed and kept: the anchor sum is exact only for a plain move.

Use: Select composite glyphs. Run the script. Choose the anchor and the masters. Press Align. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Re-aligns many marks over many masters in one Undo step.

Safety: Auto layers are listed and never edited (FontLab aligns them itself). The script refuses the whole batch, before any history exists, when:

  • a glyph has an automatic layer, or is the base of an automatic composite, also through other composites (FontLab rebuilds the composite and Undo does not restore it);

After the write, the script reads the offsets back and reports any gap. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. Use Edit > Undo then. The one-step write, the panel, the automatic-layer rule and the pending-update check are shared with other scripts (fly.ap.components.writer, fly.ap.components.panel.model, fly.ap.core.history.glyphs, fly.ap.core.edit_guards); the planner and the panel controls belong to this script.

docs.title: Build From Recipes
docs.text:
Build composite glyphs from one-line recipes with FontLab's own builder.

What: One recipe per line, for example "Aacute.alt = A + acute@acute". It attaches the "_acute" anchor of acute to the "acute" anchor of A. "a & b" places glyphs side by side; "mark@top[_top]" names both anchors. Check runs every line on every chosen master as a dry run: no outline, component, anchor or width changes (FontLab may refresh its internal glyph data), so it runs only when you press it. Build creates the glyphs, or rebuilds their layers when "Replace existing layers" is on.

How: The script hands each line to FontLab's construction engine, which validates the recipe, places the components by their anchors and sets the width. It does not compute positions itself. The result is a plain layer, never an auto layer: FontLab would notify an auto layer, and that rebuilds other auto layers in the font. An existing glyph without a layer for a chosen master gets an empty layer first (one Undo step for all such layers). A new glyph is built on the first chosen master; press Build again to build its other masters (the status line says how many are left).

Why: A recipe list is exact, repeatable and easy to review. The builder is FontLab's own, so the script does no anchor arithmetic that could disagree with FontLab.

Use: Type or paste the recipes. Choose the masters and whether to replace existing layers. Press Check, read the table, then press Build.

Benefit: Builds many composites over many masters from one reviewed list.

Undo: FontLab's builder writes each layer itself, so Edit > Undo of a rebuilt existing layer depends on FontLab; Undo of a new glyph is FontLab's Add Glyph step. Keep a saved copy of the font. The status line says how many layers were built.

Safety: Check before Build: Build stays off until every line passes. The script refuses, before any change, when:

  • an existing target glyph has an automatic layer, or is the base of an automatic composite (FontLab rebuilds the composite and Undo does not restore it);
  • a line contains a character that FontLab's text conversion can change (NUL, no-break space, line or paragraph separator).

If a build fails part-way, the error names it; the layers built before it stay. The refusal rules and the panel are shared with other scripts (fly.ap.components.writer, fly.ap.components.panel.model, fly.ap.core.history.glyphs, fly.ap.core.edit_guards); the recipe parser and the panel controls belong to this script.

Source: the author's own FontLab sample components_build_from_recipes.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

docs.title: Component Graph
docs.text:
Draw which glyphs use which other glyphs as components, as a movable graph.

What: Opens a modeless panel with a node graph of the current font. Each node is a glyph; an arrow joins a composite glyph to each glyph it uses as a component. A force layout spreads the nodes; drag a node to move it and the neighbours follow. Use it to see at a glance which base glyphs carry many composites, which glyphs sit in long dependency chains and which glyphs stand alone.

Use: Open a font. Run Components > Component Graph. Watch the layout settle, then drag nodes to explore; hover a node to see its exact glyph name. Press Refresh after you change components in the font; the graph does not follow edits by itself. The report area lists every "glyph → base" link and marks the isolated glyphs; the status line gives the reason when no graph could be built. The graph shows the components of the current master. Close the panel when you are done.

Safety: Read-only. The tool reads the component structure of the current master once per refresh. Moving a node moves only a picture in the panel. It writes no font data, selection, history, preference, file, clipboard or Output text. Closing the panel releases its scene and timers.

docs.title: Copy Offsets Between Masters
docs.text:
Copy component offsets from one master to other masters of the selected glyphs.

What: Takes the component offsets of the source master and sets them on the same components in the ticked target masters. The table shows the current and the new offset of every component that changes.

How: Components are matched by position and base glyph name. A target layer with other components, or in another order, is listed and kept. With "Scale x by advance-width ratio", the horizontal offset is multiplied by target width / source width and rounded half up, so a mark at 40 % of the width stays at 40 %. The vertical offset is copied as it is. Only the offset changes: scale, slant and the component itself stay.

Why: Composites often need the same mark placement in every master. Copying the offsets once is faster and more exact than moving marks by hand.

Use: Select composite glyphs. Run the script. Choose the source master, tick the targets. Press Copy. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

docs.title: Decompose Named Components
docs.text:
Decompose a named component subtree across selected glyphs and masters.

What: Replace occurrences of one source glyph with independent outlines. Flatten nested components inside each matched occurrence. Keep other direct components, including those with the same names as nested parts.

How: Preview matching occurrences on all masters by default. Copy each matched subtree only on Apply, before history starts, through the shared component writer. Preview reads source-layer counts without native copies. It composes the native transforms and repairs raw node connection flags, element names and notes. Keep source glyphs, anchors and metrics unchanged. Some per-node and per-contour properties are outside the shared copy helper. Each action is recorded as one Undo step. Component removal uses retained history objects; removed-component history depends on FontLab (fl#7641).

Why: Glyph > Decompose works on selected components or a whole layer. This tool adds a source-name filter, all-master preview and recursive subtree decomposition across several selected glyphs. A refused glyph or layer is listed as kept; other eligible occurrences can still change. Decompose Serif Components uses a fixed Serif prefix and removes one level; this tool uses an exact source name and flattens its complete subtree.

Use: Select composite glyphs. Run this script. Enter the exact source glyph name. Review the preview, then press Decompose. Use Reload selection after changing the selection. The panel stays open for another source name.

Benefit: Make a repeated part independent without decomposing its siblings. Automatic layers, their owners and their dependent bases are kept. Locked layers, missing bases, cyclic components and unsupported transforms are kept. Components with an interpolated # location are kept: the copy helper needs a plain source layer. Reset their locations before decomposing them here.

Credit: Independent behaviour rewrite after Fernando Díaz, Reset Type Studio, Glyphs-Scripts/Components/Decompose Specific Components (all masters).py. Repository: https://github.com/Reset-Type-Studio/Glyphs-Scripts . Source licence: Apache-2.0, declared in README.md; no LICENSE file. Copyright 2025 Fernando Díaz & Reset Type Studio. No source code was copied. Unlike the source's second name scan, nested parts are flattened only inside matched occurrences, so unrelated sibling components stay linked.

docs.title: Decompose
docs.text:
Decompose the components of the selected glyphs into plain outlines.

What: Lists every component of the selected glyphs on the chosen masters and what it becomes: the contours of its base glyph. Decompose replaces each component with editable copies of those contours, at the same place.

How: One Decompose replaces each component with the parts of its base glyph, placed by the component transform. A part that is itself a component stays a component; the table says so, and the next Decompose takes it apart too. The new contours are unlocked, as after FontLab's own Decompose. Raw node flags, element names and element notes that a native copy drops are copied back; some per-node and per-contour properties, such as corner smoothing and contour names, are not yet copied back. Auto layers are listed and kept.

Why: Decomposed outlines no longer follow later edits of the base glyph. Use it before an outline change that must be local, or for a build tool that cannot handle components. One level per press keeps every step visible.

Use: Select composite glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Decompose. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Decomposes many glyphs and masters as one Undo step, with a preview.

Safety: Auto layers are listed and never edited. The script refuses the whole batch, before any history exists, when:

  • a glyph has an automatic layer, or is the base of an automatic composite, also through other composites (FontLab rebuilds the composite and Undo does not restore it);
  • a base glyph has no plain layer for the master, holds a perspective transform or a composite shape that is not a component, or the components loop or nest more than 64 levels (the row says which).

After the write, the script reads the layers back and reports any gap. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The write is recorded as one Undo step: it hands FontLab each removed component, with its data and builder. Edit > Undo of removed components depends on FontLab (fl#7641). Replace the base glyph of matching components, and keep their placement.

What: Every component that refers to glyph X now refers to glyph Y. Offset, scale, slant, name, note and lock of each component stay. Works on the selected glyphs or on the whole font, on one or all masters. The table lists every component that changes.

How: The script sets the base glyph name of the existing component in place, then lets FontLab rebuild the component. It does not delete and re-create the component, so nothing that a re-created element would lose is lost.

Why: Swapping a mark or a figure variant in many composites by hand is slow and easy to get wrong. This keeps every placement exactly where it was.

Use: Run the script. Type the glyph to replace and the new glyph (both fields complete names). Choose the glyphs and masters. Press Replace. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Changes a component in the whole font in one Undo step.

Safety: Auto layers are listed and never edited (change their recipe). A component is blocked, with the reason in red, when:

  • the new glyph has no layer for that master;
  • the new glyph uses the edited glyph, directly or through other components (the result would refer to itself);
  • the component shares its element data with other elements (the change would reach them too).

The script refuses the whole batch, before any history exists, when:

  • a glyph has an automatic layer, or is the base of an automatic composite, also through other composites (FontLab rebuilds the composite and Undo does not restore it);

After the write, the script reads the components back and reports any gap. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. Use Edit > Undo then. The one-step write, the panel, the automatic-layer rule and the pending-update check are shared with other scripts (fly.ap.components.writer, fly.ap.components.panel.model, fly.ap.core.history.glyphs, fly.ap.core.edit_guards); the planner and the panel controls belong to this script.

docs.title: Add Extremes
docs.text:
Add on-curve nodes at the horizontal and vertical extremes of curves.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour whose curves have an extreme without a node: the node count now and the number of extremes to add. Add Extremes inserts them.

How: For each cubic curve, the script solves the derivative of x and of y for t; extremes closer than 2 % of the parameter t to an end node are ignored. FontLab's own split, flContour.insertNodeTo, inserts each node, so the curve keeps its shape up to FontLab's rounding of the new node. Cuts within 0.1 Manhattan units of an end or an earlier cut are not offered. The splits run from the last curve back, so the segment numbers of the earlier curves stay valid. TrueType (quadratic) contours and open contours are left alone.

Why: Fonts need nodes at extremes for good hinting and rasterisation, and font tests flag missing extremes. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different nodes, or when only some masters are in scope: different nodes break interpolation.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Add Extremes. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Fixes many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and keeps the masters compatible.

Safety: These shapes are listed and kept:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with scale, slant or rotation (an extreme in stored coordinates is not an extreme on screen).

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the node counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script.

Source: the author's own FontLab sample outlines_add_extremes.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

docs.title: Align And Distribute
docs.text:
Align selected geometry or space selected nodes at equal intervals.

What: Six alignment choices and horizontal or vertical node distribution share one non-modal panel. Whole selected contours move as units. Partial contours contribute selected nodes. Components move by their transform; their base glyphs stay. Anchors are never moved: this tool cannot read anchor selection. Use Contour > Align Points to align selected anchors.

How: Work in upright glyph coordinates; italic angle is not applied. Alignment uses the minimum, maximum or midpoint, or an explicit coordinate. Bounds include selected control points, so results can differ from Contour > Align Points. Component bounds use the transformed local bounding rectangle. Distribution sorts selected nodes on the chosen axis, keeps both endpoints, and divides their span equally. Ties keep contour/node order. Unselected adjacent handles follow their moved on-curve node by the same offset. Selected handles use their own targets. Node types and connection flags stay.

Why: Contour > Align Points aligns points on the current layer. Element > Align / Distribute Shapes operates on shapes. This tool adds node distribution, several glyph layers or masters in one Undo step, and a numeric preview.

Use: Select nodes or components in a Glyph window. Choose an operation, inspect the table and Apply. All nodes is for alignment only; distribution requires selected nodes. All masters processes each loaded glyph's masters; node selection is read separately in each layer. Reload selection after choosing other glyphs or editor layers. Apply reads selected layers and geometry again. A single item with Selection bounds has no move. Choose Coordinate to move it. Two selected nodes that share one curve handle are kept; select the handle too, or align them one at a time. Automatic guide/metric snapping and italic deskew are not provided.

Benefit: Repeat alignment without reopening a dialog. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Automatic-layer glyphs and their bases are skipped. Locked layers/shapes, shared node data and contours with their own transform are kept and named in the preview; the other eligible items can still change. Advances, anchors and guides stay. FontLab can round coordinates to its grid.

docs.title: Autohint Selected Layers
docs.text:
Run FontLab's PostScript autohinter on the selected glyphs, in one or all masters.

What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script runs FontLab's own autohinter on the layer. It works from the font's hinting settings (alignment zones and standard stems). The table shows the horizontal and vertical hint counts before and after. FontLab's source does not touch TrueType instructions here.

How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its hint counts, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply reads the font again and calls the native flLayer.autohint() on every planned layer, all in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. Read-back reports a layer that has an outline but no PostScript hints after the call. The hint counts and the panel are shared (fly.ap.hints.postscript, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model).

Native call caveat: FontLab's source shows that autohint switches the package master temporarily, writes hinting options and stored hinting data, and can attach hints as node links. These effects extend beyond the notified layers; the script does not check them. TrueType instructions are separate.

Why this design: - The hints come from FontLab's own autohinter, not from a script algorithm. - The script adds what the menu command does not: every master in one step, a count of hints before and after, and one Undo step. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": the change notification makes FontLab rebuild those composites, which can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. Locked layers and layers without contours are skipped. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537).

How to use: Set the alignment zones and standard stems in Font Info first. Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Autohint. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step.

Benefit: A whole selection gets fresh PostScript hints in every master, with the counts in view, in one step.

Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (hints_autohint.py, "Autohint Selected Layers").

docs.title: Correct Contour Direction
docs.text:
Set the contour direction of the selected glyphs: outer and inner contours.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every closed contour that runs the wrong way, with its current direction. Correct reverses them.

How: Native flContour.clockwise gives the direction; contains tests all segment start and mid points, as FontLab's own direction command does. Nesting within the same shape decides each edit. If layer-wide nesting would give a different answer, the contour is listed as "inside another shape, direction left" and kept. Overlapping outer contours stay outer. Native segments include TrueType implied on-curve points. PostScript outer contours run counter-clockwise; TrueType uses the opposite convention. Native flContour.reverse reverses in place.

Why: The result depends only on the shape, not on how the font was drawn, so imports and pasted outlines get the right direction. A wrong direction makes holes fill in some renderers and spoils overlap removal.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Correct. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Fixes many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and lists each wrong contour before anything changes.

Safety: Open contours have no direction and are not counted. These shapes are listed and kept, but count for the cross-shape safety check:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with scale, slant or rotation (a mirror in the transform turns the visible direction round).

After writing, a status note reports a newly introduced final off-curve with raw Smooth (fl#8517), which FontLab may change on save. Existing conditions are not reported as new. Check node types after VFJ reopen. A reversal renumbers the nodes of that contour. The panel opens with All masters chosen. When only one master has a wrong contour, check master compatibility after the change: the other masters keep their node order.

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads every direction back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script.

docs.title: Delete Duplicate Contours
docs.text:
Find contours drawn twice in the same layer and keep only the first copy.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour that repeats an earlier contour of the same layer. Delete removes the copies.

How: Two contours are duplicates when they have the same nodes in the same cyclic order, from any start node in the same direction, and each node pair lies within the tolerance (in glyph coordinates, so moved shapes compare where you see them). On-curve and off-curve nodes must match. The first contour of a group stays; FontLab's own flShape.removeContour removes the others.

Reversed duplicate groups are listed as "reversed duplicate, kept". Every member stays, including further copies: their winding can cancel. Open contours are kept; cyclic rotation changes their open endpoints.

Why: Same-direction duplicates are invisible in a filled preview, but they break overlap removal, double the ink in some renderers and confuse contour order tools. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would lose different contours, or when only some masters are in scope.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Set the tolerance and the masters. Press Delete. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Removes hidden copies over many glyphs and masters in one Undo step, and names the contour each copy repeats.

Safety: These shapes are listed and kept:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with scale, slant or rotation (stored nodes are not visible nodes).

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the contour counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script.

docs.title: Fix Zero Handles
docs.text:
Find curve handles that sit on their own node, and clean them up.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour with retracted handles: curves whose two handles both sit on their nodes, and curves with one such handle. Fix turns the first kind into lines and, when you ask for it, pulls single handles out.

How: A handle counts as retracted when it is closer than half a unit to its own node. A curve with two retracted handles is a straight line in disguise: FontLab's own flNode.convertToLine, called on the end node, removes the handles and resets the smooth flags. With "Pull single handles out to ⅓", a lone retracted handle moves a third of the way towards the other handle: the curve then has a real tangent at that node, but its shape changes slightly. TrueType (quadratic) contours are left alone.

Why: Retracted handles give a zero tangent: hinting, offsetting, stroke expansion and some rasterisers handle them badly. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different curves, or when only some masters are in scope.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the option and the masters. Press Fix. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Finds and fixes a common outline fault over many glyphs and masters in one Undo step.

Safety: Pulling a single handle on a Smooth base can leave the handles non-collinear. FontLab may later align them again. Converting a curve to a line recomputes the smooth flags at both ends. These shapes are listed and kept:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with scale, slant or rotation (stored distances are not visible distances).

A pulled handle lands on a whole unit, a third of the way to the other handle, so FontLab's rounding preference cannot move it again.

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads node counts and handle positions back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script.

docs.title: Interpolated Nudge
docs.text:
Move selected endpoints while keeping adjacent handle tension.

What: Move selected endpoints while keeping adjacent handle tension. How: Plan simultaneous moves from original coordinates. The moved node's own handles also scale. Clamp per-axis handle factors to 0 through 4; zero collapses a handle at its endpoint instead of flipping it. Tiny axis spans use rigid movement. Read-back allows 0.5 unit per axis for native rounding. Adjacent handles can lose collinearity at smooth nodes; inspect these nodes after a move. Scale each neighbouring handle about its endpoint by the changed endpoint distance in each axis. Keep ratios when an axis span is zero. Why: Adjust outlines with less handle repair. Use: Select on-curve nodes in the glyph editor, reload the panel, set X and Y, then Apply. Repeat as needed. Benefit: A repeatable non- modal nudge with one history action per Apply.

The non-modal panel previews the selected glyphs and chosen masters. Shared, scaled and rotated outline shapes are kept. Automatic-layer owners are kept. Bases of automatic composites are kept unless the shared consent option is enabled. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step through the App history writer. Reload after changing the selection.

docs.title: Myanmar Medial Ra Maker
docs.text:
Generate width-fitted Myanmar medial-ra variants on every FontLab master.

What: Group consonants on the current master. Fit the same group members on all masters, using each master's mean advance minus its own template enclosure. Names use the current master's group means floored to tens. Also create eight unstretched omission variants. Existing names and targets with a bad master are kept, with the master and reason listed. How: Read U+1000–U+1020 by Unicode or hexadecimal name. Verify the five pieces: stem, top rail, top hook, bottom rail, bottom hook. The stem must be tallest; top pieces above bottom pieces; hooks right of rails. The rails' closing edges must be on their right, the hooks' on their left. Copy through the shared App contour copier. Show every target's extension and node/handle bounds on every master in the Preview table. Apply refuses source data changed since Preview. Why: Fit this five-part Myanmar outline to consonant width groups. All-master output keeps the generated glyph structure consistent across masters; a failed template keeps the entire target. Use: Select one template, or leave the selection empty to use U+103C. Inspect Preview and consent to any listed automatic-glyph rebuilds, then Apply. Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step. Benefit: Produce a compatible set of fitted medial-ra variants for refinement.

docs.title: Optimize Start Points
docs.text:
Move the start node of every closed contour to its bottom-left on-curve node.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour whose start node moves, and the node that becomes the start. Optimize applies the moves.

How: The bottom-left node is the lowest on-curve node; on a tie, the leftmost one. "Match current master" finds it in the current master and uses the same node number in every other master whose contour has the same node count, so the masters stay compatible. "Bottom-left in each master" finds it in each master on its own. FontLab's own flContour.setStartPoint turns the node list round in place; this is meant to keep the node flags. docs.title: Outline Effect
docs.text:
Turn the selected glyphs into outlined (hollow) letters of a chosen line width.

What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script replaces the contours of the layer with a ring of the chosen line width, centred on the old outline. The advance width does not change.

How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its contour count, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply first builds every ring: Qt's path stroker draws the contours with round joins and caps, the script turns the stroke into closed FontLab contours (cubic handles stay cubic), and FontGate's Remove Overlap cleans the small loops that the stroker leaves inside corners. Then it writes all layers in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs: each old contour element is removed and the ring is added as one new element. Images and empty elements stay in the layer. After the write it counts the contours again and reports any difference. The path-to-contour step and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.copy, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model).

Why this design: - FontLab has no Python call that strokes an outline, so the script uses the Qt stroker and FontLab's own overlap removal. FontGate puts the result on the integer grid. - The geometry is built before history starts, so a failed stroke never leaves a half-edited layer. - Layers with components are skipped: the components would stay filled. Locked layers are skipped too. Element names and notes of the old outline do not carry over to the ring. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": FontLab then rebuilds those composites, can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537).

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Set the line width, choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Outline. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step.

Benefit: An inline or outline style starts from the real drawing, in every master, in one step.

The script creates one empty glyph per entry, with a layer on every master and the chosen advance width. A single non-ASCII character becomes uniXXXX (or uXXXXX) and gets that code point. A name of that form also gets its code point, unless another glyph has it already. ASCII tokens are glyph names: A stays A; & and 1 are invalid names.

How it works: A small non-modal panel shows a live table: the name, the code point and what will happen. Existing glyphs, repeated entries and invalid names are listed and skipped. Create checks the font again. FontLab's own Add Glyph command makes each new glyph with a layer on every master, the advance width and the code point (shared module fly.ap.glyphs.creation). After the write the script reads every new glyph back, and checks that no automatic glyph of the font changed.

Why this design: - Placeholders let you build features, classes, kerning groups and test strings before the drawings exist. Unlike Font > Add Glyphs, the panel takes characters directly, previews every name and code point, and skips what exists instead of asking. - An existing glyph is never overwritten, and a code point that another glyph has is never assigned twice. - FontLab's text conversion can change some characters, so the script refuses text with NUL, no-break space or the Unicode line and paragraph separators instead of creating changed names. - A code point write needs an active Font window and no open Glyph window, as every Unicode writer of this menu does. Create discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). - FontLab can rebuild an automatic glyph when a new name appears. When the font has automatic glyphs without a recipe whose names share a dotted suffix with a new name (a new e.sc and eacute.sc), the row shows "may rebuild auto ..." and is skipped unless you tick "Create even if FontLab may rebuild these auto glyphs". A change of the text clears the tick. - Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step.

How to use: Open a font and activate its Font window. Run the script. Type the names or characters, set the advance width, check the table and press Create.

Benefit: A complete glyph set skeleton, named and encoded, in seconds.

docs.title: Remove Overlap
docs.text:
Remove overlaps in the outline shapes of the selected glyphs.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every outline shape whose contours overlap: the contour count now and after the merge. Remove Overlap merges them. Shapes without overlap stay untouched. Overlaps between separate shapes are not merged. This tool tests intersections between contours; a single self-intersecting contour is kept.

How: Each shape goes through FontLab's FontGate engine: a copy is made with flShape.convertToFgShape, fgShape.removeOverlap merges it (a shape has an overlap when native contours intersect or same-direction contours nest), and flShape.assign writes the result back into the same shape object. The start node of each new contour moves back to an old start point when one survives the merge, as FontLab's own command does. The preview runs the same merge on a copy, so the numbers are exact.

Why: Overlapping contours print and render fine in many places, but fonts for the web, variable fonts and many tools need clean outlines. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different contours, or when only some masters are in scope: the merge would break interpolation.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Choose the masters. Press Remove Overlap. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Cleans many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and lists each merge before anything changes.

Safety: A status note reports only a newly introduced final off-curve with raw Smooth (fl#8517), which FontLab may change on save. Check node types after VFJ reopen. The merge rebuilds the contours of a merged shape: node names, node flags, contour names and corner_smooth (fl#8569) in that shape are not kept. FontGate assign also replaces the shape appearance. No name, note or appearance preservation is claimed for that round trip. These shapes are listed and kept:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with a transform (FontGate would merge them in stored coordinates);
  • shapes with an open contour (an open contour has no inside).

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the contour counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script.

Source: the author's own FontLab sample outlines_remove_overlap.py, Apache-2.0. Adapted for the current FontLab 9 API.

Run Contours > Remove Overlap from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Round Coordinates
docs.text:
Round node coordinates, anchors and component offsets to a grid.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table shows how many nodes are off the grid and which component offsets change. Round snaps them to the nearest multiple of the grid (1 unit by default).

How: A node is rounded in glyph coordinates. When its shape is moved (a plain shape offset), the script rounds the visible position and stores the matching local value, so the node lands on the grid where you see it. Halves round up (2.5 -> 3, -2.5 -> -2), as Qt's qRound and Anchors > Round To Grid do. Component offsets are rounded; the scale and slant of a component stay. Nodes are moved in place, which is meant to keep node names and flags (FontLab’s source; not measured).

Why: Scaling, interpolation and imports leave fractional or off-grid coordinates. They cost file size and can cause rendering noise. Optional anchor rounding uses fly.ap.anchors.writer in the same transaction. A layer with ambiguous anchor names or an existing anchor that would move to 0, 0 is listed and kept (fl#8527).

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Set the grid and the masters; untick "Component offsets" to keep them. Anchors starts ticked; untick Anchors to round only nodes and offsets. Press Round. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Cleans many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, and shows the count before anything changes.

Safety: These shapes are listed and kept:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with scale, slant or rotation (their stored grid is not the visible grid);
  • shapes moved by a fraction of a unit (FontLab may round the stored nodes, so the visible nodes could not land on the grid).

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads every value back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. The one-step write, the automatic-layer rule, the pending-update check and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.writer, fly.ap.contours.panel.model); the planner belongs to this script.
