docs.title: Shadow Copy
docs.text:
Add a shifted copy of the outline behind each selected glyph, as its own element.

What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, the script copies the contours of the layer, moves the copy by a horizontal and a vertical offset, and puts it behind the outline as a new element named "shadow". The original outline and the advance width do not change.

How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with its contour count, or the reason why the layer is skipped. Apply reads the font again and writes all layers in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. The copy is made from each contour with its element transform applied; FontLab can drop node names and raw node flags in a contour copy (fl#8569), so the script copies them back and clears the selection bit. After the write it checks that every layer starts with the shadow element and reports any difference. The contour copy and the panel are shared (fly.ap.contours.copy, fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model).

Copy limits: Only node names and raw node flags are repaired (fl#8569); selection is cleared. Other node properties and contour names are not repaired. Copied contours are merged into one element; source element names and notes are not copied.

Why this design: - A separate element is easy to recolour, move or delete as one unit, and a layer font workflow can split it into shadow glyphs. Filled together with the outline it gives an extruded silhouette. - Layers with components are skipped: a copy of the contours alone would not be the full glyph. Locked layers and layers that already hold a shadow element are skipped too. - Automatic layers and glyphs with automatic layers are never edited. A base of automatic composites is skipped unless you tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway": FontLab then rebuilds those composites, can drop their anchors and locks, and Undo does not restore them. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The script does not call UpdateAll (fl#8537). The panel binds to the font that was current when it opened.

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Set the offsets, choose the current master or all masters, check the table and press Add Shadow. The panel stays open; press "Use selection" after you select other glyphs. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step.

Benefit: Shadowed or extruded display styles start from the real outline in one step, and the shadow stays a separate element.

docs.title: Small Caps From Capitals
docs.text:
Create small-cap glyphs (h.sc, a.sc, ...) from the selected capitals.

What it does: For each selected capital the script creates a small-cap glyph on every master: H becomes h.sc, H.ss01 becomes h.sc.ss01. The outline is scaled by separate horizontal and vertical factors; the advance width is scaled horizontally. The capitals do not change.

How it works: A non-modal panel lists every selected glyph with its new name, or the reason why it is skipped. Create checks the font again. FontLab's own Add Glyph command makes each new glyph with its master layers and widths (rounded half up). Then one step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs adds the scaled copies to all new layers. The copy keeps node names and raw node flags, which a FontLab contour copy can drop (fl#8569). After the write the script reads every new layer back, and checks that no automatic glyph of the font changed. Other node properties and contour names are not repaired. Copied contours are merged into one element; source element names and notes are not copied.

Why this design: - The name is the lowercase base plus ".sc", the usual naming for the smcp and c2sc features. - A larger horizontal than vertical factor keeps vertical stems relatively heavier, so the small caps do not look too light at once. When the font has automatic glyphs without a recipe whose names carry the new suffix (such as eacute.sc), the row shows "may rebuild auto ..." and is skipped unless you tick "Create even if FontLab may rebuild these auto glyphs". Use selection clears the tick. - Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step.

docs.title: Smart Slant
docs.text:
Slant outlines and compensate the change in their horizontal bounds.

What: Apply a slant, then preserve sidebearings or the original ink centre. How: Measure the actual cubic bounds before and after the shear. Keeping sidebearings aligns the left ink edge and adjusts advance by the ink-width change. Centre mode keeps advance and centres the new ink on the old ink. Why: A plain shear can shift the drawing within its advance. Compensation gives a controlled starting point for an italic, across selected masters. Native Tools > Transform > Slant, Slant by Italic Angle and Actions > Oblique do not provide this spacing compensation. Scripts/Contours/Slant.py keeps the advance unchanged. This tool keeps both sidebearings by adjusting the advance, or keeps the original ink centre at unchanged advance. Use: Select glyphs, run this panel, choose angle and spacing mode, inspect the preview, then Slant. Positive angles lean right. Reload new selections. Benefit: Repeat the same optical placement over glyphs of different heights.

Anchors follow the same matrix when enabled. Guides and metric expressions stay. Components, open contours and locked shapes are kept and listed; other glyphs can still be edited. Automatic glyphs and their bases follow the panel's geometry policy. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. FontLab can round the baked coordinates. Font italic-angle metadata is not changed by this drawing tool.

docs.title: Straighten Short Curves
docs.text:
Turn short, flat curves into straight lines.

What: For each selected glyph and master, the table lists every contour with curves that are short and flat: the number of curves now, how many become lines, and the largest handle deviation. Straighten converts them.

How: A cubic curve qualifies when its chord is no longer than "Chord up to" and both handles lie within "Handles within" of the chord, between its ends. FontLab's own flNode.convertToLine, called on the end node of the curve, removes the two handles and recomputes the smooth flags at both ends. TrueType (quadratic) contours are left alone.

Why: Autotracing and format conversion leave tiny curves that are really lines. As lines they hint better, interpolate more safely and take less space. With "Keep masters compatible" ticked, a glyph is held back when the masters would get different curves, or when only some masters are in scope.

Use: Select glyphs. Run the script. Set the two limits and the masters. Press Straighten. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

Benefit: Cleans many glyphs over many masters in one Undo step, with the worst deviation shown before anything changes.

Safety: These shapes are listed and kept:

  • shared outline data (an edit would change other glyphs too);
  • shapes with scale, slant or rotation (stored lengths are not visible lengths).

A glyph that has an automatic layer is listed and skipped. So is a glyph that is a base of an automatic composite, also through other composites, unless you tick "Also edit bases of automatic composites" (FontLab then rebuilds those composites; Undo may not restore their anchors). The script keeps the compatibility check; writes disclose queued ids and possible date changes. After the write, it reads the node counts back. If FontLab fails part-way, the error says that native changes may remain. The change is recorded as one Undo step. docs.title: TGlyph Window
docs.text:

docs.title: Generate Random Alternates Feature
docs.text:
Generate seeded contextual alternate feature source for the current font.

What: Build random context classes and substitution lookups from user-supplied base/alternate rows. Keep the seed to reproduce exactly the same source. How: Read the current glyph catalogue. Assign category members to nonempty classes, then choose a target and context for each rule using a local RNG. Why: OpenType contextual substitutions are deterministic. Random generation makes varied rules; it does not make the shaping engine choose randomly. The native Features editor accepts source, but does not generate seeded contexts. Write feature replaces the code for the previewed feature tag only after Replace existing feature is ticked for a differing block. Preview shows existing and generated code side by side. Adding a tag or writing identical code needs no confirmation. Changing input or refreshing resets the tick. The shared source-bound writer preserves other features and the prefix stay unchanged. Each changing write is recorded as one Undo step. Compile and test in FontLab's Features panel after writing. Benefit: Review and reproduce varied alternates without manual rule entry. The non-modal panel shows the exact block that Write feature stores. The category filter uses Unicode general categories, with base-name inheritance for suffix glyphs; unencoded names without an encoded base match only All. Export flags are not used. Classes stay inside the generated feature block.

docs.title: Master Metrics Table
docs.text:
Edit ascender, descender, x-height and cap-height across masters; diagram follows the selected row.

What it does: Open with a font active. Double-click a metric value, check the selected row's diagram, then choose Apply. Every row is checked before any edit. Apply writes all changed masters as one Undo step and preserves glyph outlines. Keep this panel bound to its original font; reopen it after switching to another font.

How it works: Read each master's four vertical metrics while restoring the original current master. Validate finite, ordered, signed-16-bit proposals before writing metadata. Apply refuses when a value changed since the preview. It then writes and reads back each changed master. When one master fails, the written values are restored and nothing is added to Undo. When a restore also fails, the status names each failure (such as "master Bold was not restored") and says that values can remain; check every master before you save.

Why this design: A complete multi-row proposal prevents a later invalid cell from leaving an earlier master partially updated by normal validation.

How to use: Activate the font's Font window and run Font Info > Master Metrics Table. Edit metric cells, select a row to inspect its diagram and press Apply after reviewing every master. Use Edit > Undo in the Font window to revert the whole Apply. Reopen after changing fonts.

Benefit: Stage family-wide vertical metrics together while keeping glyph outlines unchanged.

docs.text:

docs.title: Trial Font Maker
docs.text:
Make prefixed trial copies of static fonts exported from the current font.

What: Keep selected FontLab glyphs in each matching exported OTF or TTF. Keep .notdef and component dependencies. Ligature expansion is off by default; tick Also keep ligatures to include the extra glyphs listed in the preview. Keep kerning and positioning unless Remove kerning and positioning is ticked. Keep the existing liga substitutions that survive this keep set. Prefix family, full, unique and PostScript names, including CFF names. Preserve copyright and licence records. How: Read exported binaries with fontTools, subset detached copies and save new files. Inspect the saved copies by reopening them in FontLab. No source font or source binary is edited. There is no font edit and no Undo step. Why: File > Export Font As produces the source binaries. This panel adds a selected glyph keep set and consistent trial names across those static exports. It avoids changing a live font or relying on Glyphs export-only custom parameters. Usage: Export static OTF/TTF instances to a folder first. Select the trial glyphs in FontLab. Open this panel, enter that folder, a different output folder and a prefix. Inspect the per-file preview, then press Make Trial Copies. Use selection reads the glyph selection again. Family name and UPM must match the current font; other files get named kept rows. Existing destinations are kept. Variable fonts are kept: export static instances before using this tool. Benefit: Repeatable trial binaries without deleting work from the design source. The keep set uses exported glyph names. Preserve glyph names in the export profile; renamed or absent glyphs are reported instead of silently dropped. Substitution features are limited to liga and the retained positioning feature tags; ligatures are not invented. Requires user-installed fontTools in FontLab's Python site-packages, such as the dependency installed with fontlab-fontport. FontLab's private copy is not used. Install it through Settings > Python if it is missing. Source inspection is cached until the folder or selection changes, or Refresh Exports is pressed. Prefix edits update destination names without opening fonts.

Independent behaviour rewrite of Fernando Díaz / Reset Type Studio, Glyphs-Scripts/Exports/Trial Font Maker.py. https://github.com/Reset-Type-Studio/Glyphs-Scripts Apache-2.0, declared in the repository README; no separate LICENSE file. No source code was copied.

docs.title: Suggest Zones From Overshoots
docs.text:
Suggest alignment zones from the overshoots of H, O, x and o, then apply them.

What it does: For each chosen master, measures H and O at the baseline and the cap height, and x and o at the x-height. A zone starts at the edge of the flat letter (H or x). Its width is the distance that the round letter (O or o) passes that edge: upward for the cap-height and x-height zones, downward for the baseline zone. The table shows every suggested zone and the zone that it replaces. Apply writes the previewed zones of all chosen masters as one Undo step. This tool reads the four glyphs and does not edit them.

How it works: A suggested zone replaces the existing zone of the same kind at the same position; otherwise the zone with the same name; otherwise it is added. A replaced zone keeps its name, tags and lock. All other zones stay. The zones are written through the shared native zone backend, the route of Metrics > Alignment Zones. Apply first measures the four glyphs again and refuses when they changed since the preview. The extents come from the outline geometry (nodes and exact curve extremes, components placed), because FontLab's cached glyph box can be stale after an edit (fl#8575).

Why this design: The preview shows the exact zones before any write, and one shared zone writer keeps the refusals and the Undo step the same in every zone tool.

How to use: Open a font, activate its Font window and run Guides > Suggest Zones From Overshoots. Choose the current master or all masters, review the table and press Apply. Press Refresh after you edit the glyphs or the zones. Use Edit > Undo in the Font window to revert the whole Apply.

Benefit: Set zones that match the real overshoots of every master in one reviewed step.

Limitations: - A missing glyph or layer, or a layer with no height, gives no zone for the rules that need it. The status line names them. - A glyph whose outline cannot be read (for example a segment with one cubic control) is listed as not measured, with the reason; the other glyphs are still measured. - Stroke thickness is not counted: zones measure the outline. - The Undo step is named "Alignment Zones", like the zone panel's. - Apply needs the Font window of this font as the active window. It refuses while a Glyph window is the active canvas. - Apply re-creates every zone guide of a changed master (new ids, x-centre 0, font guideline style), as Font Info does. - FontLab defect fl#8574: after Edit > Undo or Redo, the metric guides show 3 of 9 lines until you reopen the font. The saved file is correct.

Credit: Adapted from zones_from_glyphs.py, the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0.

Run Guides > Suggest Zones From Overshoots from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Copy Layer Between Masters
docs.text:
Copy the outline, anchors and advance width from one master to others.

What it does: For each selected glyph, replace the contours of the target master layers with copies of the contours of the source master layer. Optionally move same-named anchors to the source positions and set the source advance width. Components of the targets stay; components of the source are not copied.

How it works: A non-modal panel has a "From" master, checked target masters, and two options: Anchors and Advance width. The table shows, per target layer, contours now and after, width now and after. Copy reads the font again and writes every target in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. The old outline shapes of a target are removed (empty ones too) and repaired clones of the source outline shapes are added. After the write the script reads contour counts, widths and anchor positions back and reports any difference.

Why this design: - The target loses its outline shapes, it never edits them. A shape that other glyphs share stays intact for them. - FontLab clone() drops shape notes and names and the raw state and name of nodes (fl#8516, fl#8538). The script copies them back, clears selection bits, and stops when a clone has another contour count. - Only same-named anchors move; missing anchors are listed, never added. Two anchors with one name make the layer ambiguous: it is skipped. An existing anchor that would move to 0, 0 is skipped too: FontLab does not Redo that move (fl#8527). - Skipped and listed: automatic layers, glyphs with automatic layers, bases of automatic composites (also through manual composites), locked layers, layers with a metrics link or expression, and a source without outline. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The panel binds to the font that was current when it opened.

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Pick the source master and the targets. Changing the source checks all other masters again. Check the table. Press Copy. Then check the masters for compatibility: the targets now have the point structure of the source.

Benefit: Start the outlines of a new master from an existing one, or resync the outlines of a broken master, in one step and one Undo.

Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (masters_copy_layer.py, "Copy Layer Between Masters"). Known limit: node.clone loses explicit corner smoothness and other scalar node properties (fl#8569); a shape clone may lose them too.

docs.title: Copy Outline To Mask
docs.text:
Copy the outline of each selected glyph into the mask of its master layer.

What it does: For each selected glyph and chosen master, put a copy of the contours of the master layer into its mask (background) layer. The mask is created when it is missing. "Replace mask" removes what the mask holds first; "Add to mask" keeps it. The master layer does not change.

How it works: A non-modal panel lists every glyph and master with three numbers: contours in the outline, contours in the mask now (plus its components, which "Replace mask" also removes), contours in the mask after the copy. Apply reads the font again, then writes all masks in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. Existing masks join the history list before the edit; new masks join the notification as created objects. "Replace mask" removes the old mask shapes one by one. The shape, shape data and builder of each removed component are read before the edit and retained in the notification. The removal is recorded as one Undo step. After the write the script counts the mask contours again, checks that no old component is left, and reports any difference.

Why this design: - Only contours are copied. Components stay in the body: a mask is a drawing reference, and a component in a mask would follow later edits of its base glyph. - Each outline shape is cloned whole, so its own transform stays. FontLab clone() drops shape notes and names and the raw state and name of nodes (fl#8516, fl#8538). The script copies them back, and clears selection bits: a mask must not look selected. A clone with another contour count stops the run. - Edit > Undo of removed components depends on FontLab (fl#7641). - Automatic layers, glyphs with automatic layers, bases of automatic composites (also through manual composites) and locked layers are listed and skipped. A notification there makes FontLab rebuild the automatic glyphs, and Undo does not restore them. - Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The panel binds to the font that was current when it opened.

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the current master or all masters, and the mode. Check the table. Press Copy. The panel stays open; press "Use selection" after you select other glyphs.

Benefit: A reference copy of the current drawing behind every glyph, before a redesign, in one step and one Undo.

Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (masters_copy_to_mask.py, "Copy Outline to Mask"). Known limit: node.clone loses explicit corner smoothness and other scalar node properties (fl#8569); a shape clone may lose them too.

docs.title: Deliver Glyphs
docs.text:
Deliver selected outline glyphs to the font you activate next.

What: Keep a source font and glyph selection in a non-modal panel. Activate a destination font, preview master pairing, then Deliver. Repeat for other open fonts. Outlines, anchors, advances and metrics expressions then travel in one geometry action through outline_writer and anchor_writer. Why: Native copy and paste also transfers components and hints; this tool adds retained source selection, master-name pairing and visible fallbacks across repeated destinations. Named contours and nodes with an explicit corner_smooth value are kept. Other node and contour properties are not detected and not copied (fl#8569). Nothing is saved. docs.title: Display Next Layer
docs.text:
Show the next layer of each selected glyph in the Glyph window.

What it does: Cycle the displayed layer of the selected glyph slot(s) to the next layer of the same master. After the last layer, wrap to the first one.

How it works: FontLab binds a layer to a master by its name. The text before the first "@" (or "#") identifies master and alternate layers. Backups use backup ; legacy @ and space-prefixed backups also take part, resolved by the longest master prefix. Masks and service layers stay out. The script reads the shown layer of each selected slot, lists the glyph layers of the same master in glyph order, and picks the next one. A slot with an explicit layer name gets the new name. A slot that follows the active layer gets a new active layer for its glyph.

Why this design: - fly.ap.masters.inspect.model.associated_master resolves native layer names; the same backup resolver as Restore Backup Layer adds plain backup names. - All slots are planned first. One bad slot stops the run before any change. - The script writes no font data. No Undo step is needed.

How to use: Open a Glyph window. Select a glyph. Run the script. Assign a shortcut to this script and to "Display Previous Layer" to walk through backups fast.

Benefit: One key press compares master, backup and alternate layers in place.

Credit: Behaviour after Pedro Arilla's Glyphs script "Display next layer" (Apache-2.0). Independent rewrite. No source code was copied.

docs.title: Layer Cleanup
docs.text:
List the extra layers of the selected glyphs and delete the ticked ones.

What it does: Fonts collect masks, backups, alternates and experiment layers. The panel lists every non-master layer of the selected glyphs with its kind and contour count. Tick rows one by one, or tick a whole kind with one button. "Delete Ticked" removes the ticked layers.

How it works: The kind comes from the layer role, fly.ap.masters.inspect.model.associated_master, and the same backup resolver as Restore Backup Layer: "mask" for a background; "backup" for backup and legacy @ or space-prefixed backups; "alternate" for #... layers, such as bracket layers; "other" for every other layer. Master layers, service layers, image layers and temporary "|temp|" layers are never listed. The delete runs in one Undo step through the shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs. FontLab records the step only for layers plus their glyph, so the notification holds a layer that stays: the body layer of a deleted mask, else the first master layer. The script then checks by layer id that every ticked layer is gone.

Why this design: - Nothing is ticked at the start. A delete is explicit. - The shown (active) layer of a glyph and locked layers are listed but cannot be ticked: FontLab would have to pick another shown layer, and a lock is a deliberate "keep". - Glyphs with automatic layers and bases of automatic composites (also through manual composites) are listed but cannot be ticked. A notification there makes FontLab rebuild the automatic glyphs, and Undo does not restore them. - A deleted body layer leaves its mask. The mask has its own row: tick both to remove both. - The components of the deleted layers (shape, shape data, builder) are read before the edit and retained in the notification. The deletion is recorded as one Undo step. Edit > Undo of removed components depends on FontLab (fl#7641). - To clear the backgrounds of the whole font, use Cleanup > Clear All Layer Backgrounds or Clear Master Backgrounds: they check the whole font mapping first. This panel is for mixed cleanup of a selection. - Delete discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. The panel binds to the font that was current when it opened.

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window (Select All for the whole font). Run the script. Tick rows or press a kind button. Press Delete Ticked. The deletion is recorded as one Undo step.

Benefit: A clean Layers panel and a smaller file, without clicking through every glyph.

docs.title: Select Different Colour
docs.text:
Add to the Font window selection all glyphs of a different mark colour.

What it does: Read the mark colours of the selected glyphs. Then select, in addition, every glyph whose mark colour is none of those colours. Unmarked glyphs count as one colour of their own. With no selection, do nothing.

How it works: The script reads the Font window selection, collects the mark values of the selected glyphs, and selects all other glyphs whose mark is not in that set. The old selection stays. It changes only the selection, never a glyph.

Why this design: - Pairs with "Select by Mark". That script picks colours from a list. This one derives the colours from the current selection: select a few glyphs of the colour to keep, run the script, then delete or move the rest. - It uses the shared selection helper, which refuses to write the selection while a Glyph window is active (FontLab bug fl#8528). - Difference to the Glyphs original: it works on all glyphs of the font. The displayed-list accessors are not exposed by the inspected PythonQt API. Filtered-view equivalence remains unverified.

How to use: Open the Font window. Select glyphs of the colour(s) to keep apart. Run the script. Press Backspace or drag the selection as you need.

Benefit: Split a font by colour labels in two clicks.

Credit: Behaviour after Pedro Arilla's Glyphs script "Select different colour" (Apache-2.0), which is based on "Select Different Color" by Rainer Erich Scheichelbauer (mekkablue, Apache-2.0). Independent rewrite. No source code was copied.

Run Masters > Select Different Colour from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Selection Layer Navigator
docs.text:
Compare selected glyph slots by layer name or by one design axis.

What: A non-modal navigator with Previous and Next. Layer order uses the first usable selected slot to choose one name for all selected slots, across masters and auxiliary layers. Skip locked layers in this mode. An unusable reference gets a named kept row; the next usable slot supplies the reference instead. Axis mode moves each slot to its next coordinate while keeping all other axis coordinates fixed. Wrap at either end. Italic / Slant selects the first axis tagged ital or slnt. All font axes are available.

How: Read the live selection on each click through App. Explicit text-block layer names stay explicit, so repeated glyphs can show different layers. Slots without an explicit layer name continue to follow the glyph's active layer. Changing that active layer also affects other following slots of that glyph. Read native master positions for intermediate layers; keep layers without complete coordinates. In a Font window, axis mode changes the current font master. Layer order needs a Glyph window. Missing or ambiguous targets produce named kept rows. No outlines, metrics, preferences or font history are written.

Why: Native Layer > Next (Alt+.) and Layer > Previous (Alt+,) navigate the active glyph only and skip locked layers. This panel adds selection-only synchronization, axis filtering, reverse travel and per-slot results. Master Switcher chooses a named master; this tool finds the next related coordinate instead. Display Next Layer and Display Previous Layer cycle each glyph's backups separately within one master.

Usage: Open a font. Run the tool, select glyph slots in a Glyph window, choose Layer order or an axis, then click Previous or Next. Each click reads the live selection. After changing fonts, click Use Current Font. The result area lists every changed or kept slot. Close releases the panel's signal connections.

Benefit: Compare matching drawings while keeping explicit unselected slots fixed.

Credit: Alex Slobzheninov, https://github.com/slobzheninov/Glyphs-Scripts, Apache-2.0, copyright 2020 Alex Slobzheninov. Independent behaviour rewrite of App/Next Layer in Selection.py, Previous Layer in Selection.py, Toggle Axis 1.py through Toggle Axis 4.py, Toggle Italic.py and ToggleAxis.py. No source code, identifiers or comments were copied beyond public API names.

Run Masters > Selection Layer Navigator from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Selection To All Backgrounds
docs.text:
Copy the selected contours into the background of every glyph.

What it does: Take the selected contours of the shown glyph layer. Replace the background (mask layer) of the current-master layer of EVERY glyph in the font with copies of them. Use it to put one guide shape, such as a grid or a reference skeleton, behind all glyphs.

How it works: A contour counts as selected when all its nodes are selected (select a contour with a double click, or drag a box around it). A panel first shows what will happen: contour count, glyph count, backgrounds to be replaced and glyphs to be skipped. The panel stays open. "Refresh" in a Glyph window reads the selection again; when nothing is selected there, it clears the preview and turns off the button. "Refresh" in the Font window reads the planned contours again. Switch to the Font window, then press "Replace backgrounds". It reads the planned contours and the font again and stops if anything changed. Then it removes the old background shapes, creates missing backgrounds, and adds clones of the selected contours. One notification covers the whole font: one Undo step in the Font window. The shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs decides which glyphs are skipped and does the one-step write. Read-back checks every target background for the planned contour count and no components. A mismatch is reported with the Edit > Undo hint.

Why this design: - The change spans the whole font and overwrites backgrounds. So there is a preview and an explicit button; there is no silent run. - The write runs only while the Font window is active. While a Glyph window is active, FontLab records the Undo step for the shown glyph only: Edit > Undo then restores that glyph and leaves the other backgrounds changed (measured on FontLab 9.0.9790). Edit > Undo in a Glyph window after the write also undoes only the shown glyph. - The panel works only on the current master. Other masters keep their backgrounds. - Glyphs with an automatic layer, glyphs that are a base of one (also through manual composites), glyphs with a locked master layer and glyphs without a layer for the current master are skipped and counted. An automatic layer must never be notified: it would rebuild every automatic glyph. In a font with many recipes, most base letters are skipped. - FontLab clone() drops shape notes and names and the raw state and name of nodes. The script copies them back, except selection bits. - Only contours move. Components in the selection are not copied.

How to use: Open a Glyph window. Select the contours. Run the script. Read the summary. Switch to the Font window. Click "Replace backgrounds". Use Edit > Undo in the Font window to revert.

Benefit: One reference shape behind the whole font in one step.

Credit: Behaviour after Pedro Arilla's Glyphs script "Selection to all the backgrounds" (Apache-2.0). Independent rewrite. No source code was copied. Known limit: clone() recalculates smooth flags (fl#8516); the script restores node states.

Run Masters > Selection To All Backgrounds from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Set Intermediate Layer
docs.text:
Add interpolated intermediate layers to selected glyphs at explicit coordinates.

What: Preview one new intermediate layer per selected glyph. Set each axis coordinate in design units, then press Add Layers. Existing layers stay. How: FontLab interpolates each glyph with interpolateInstance. The result gets a location name such as :wt=512.5 and is added through shared history.commit. The change is recorded as one Undo step. No glyph or font master is created. Why: FontLab's Layers and Masters panel can add a layer and Glyph > Reinterpolate can fill it. This panel combines the two over a selection, with a refusal report. Use: Open a font with at least two masters and declared axes. Select glyphs, run the tool, set coordinates and inspect the preview before adding layers. Benefit: Build matching intermediate locations without repeating layer setup.

Automatic glyphs and their bases, locked sources, incompatible masters, existing locations and fonts without declared axes are kept. Editor tabs and their order stay in place; this tool does not replace displayed glyph slots. Fractional coordinates are preserved. Invalid values are refused.

Independent behaviour rewrite after Reza Bohloul, RezaBohloul, Glyph/Set Intermediate Layer.py; no licence declared. Repository: https://github.com/RezaBohloul/RezaBohloul . No source code copied.

Open every foreground layer of the selected glyph occurrences in a proof.

docs.title: Sync Sidebearings
docs.text:
Copy sidebearings from a reference master to the other masters.

What it does: For each selected glyph, give the layers of the other masters the left and right sidebearings of the reference master. "Proportional to ink width" scales the reference sidebearings by the ratio of the ink widths (target / reference), so bolder masters keep the same rhythm. "Same values" copies them unchanged. The outline, components and anchors move together, and the advance width follows.

How it works: The ink edges are the outline bounding box. New LSB and RSB are rounded half up to whole units. The script moves the layer by the LSB change and sets the advance width to new LSB + ink width + new RSB. The panel is the shared Metrics panel (fly.ap.metrics.panel.model): a live preview table, the masters choice (the current master or all masters; the reference itself is never a target), one Undo step per Apply and a read-back of advance and outline edge.

Why this design: - The shared panel moves outlines in place (applyTransform), never through a clone, so node flags and shape notes stay (fl#8516, fl#8538). - Automatic layers and glyphs that own one are listed and skipped. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped: the link would undo the change. A base of automatic composites needs the "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" tick, because FontLab rebuilds the automatic glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. - A glyph without outline in the reference or the target is listed and skipped: it has no sidebearings. - Values round half up, not to the nearest even number: 52.5 becomes 53.

How to use: Space the reference master first. Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the reference and the rule. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open; press "Use selection" for other glyphs.

Benefit: Consistent spacing across all masters in one step, as a start for fine-tuning the extremes.

Credit: Adapted from the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0 (masters_sync_metrics.py, "Sync Sidebearings").

Run Masters > Sync Sidebearings from FontLab's Scripts menu.

Read installation and working with scripts before use.

docs.title: Transform Background
docs.text:
Scale or shift the background of the selected glyph layers.

What it does: Open a small floating panel with two actions. "Scale" multiplies the background of every selected glyph layer by a percentage, around the origin (0, 0). "Shift" moves the background horizontally by a number of units. Positive units move right, negative units move left.

How it works: The background of a FontLab layer is its mask layer. The script finds it with getMaskLayer(False), so it never creates a background. Layers without one are skipped. It then applies one transform to the mask layer: contours, components and anchors move together. Metrics and guides of the mask stay. FontLab rounds the result as set in the preferences. One notification covers all backgrounds: one Undo step per click.

Why this design: - One panel replaces the two Glyphs scripts. It stays open, so you can scale, shift and repeat while you compare with the foreground. - The Glyphs scripts read a number from a text box once per run and close. They break on invalid input. This panel checks the number and shows the reason in the status line. - The Glyphs scale script ignores components. This script moves them too. - A glyph that has an automatic layer, or is a base of one (also through manual composites), is refused: FontLab cannot undo an edit that reaches an automatic layer. So is a click while FontLab has pending glyph updates. The shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs does these checks and the one-step write. - Zero, negative, empty and non-finite scale values are refused. A scale of 0 would destroy the background; a negative scale would mirror it.

How to use: Select glyphs in the Font window, or open a Glyph window. Type a number. Press Return or click the button. Use Edit > Undo to revert.

Benefit: Fit a traced or imported background to your drawing without redrawing it.

Credit: Behaviour after Pedro Arilla's Glyphs scripts "Scale background in selected glyphs" and "Shift background in selected glyphs" (Apache-2.0). Independent rewrite. No source code was copied.

Run Masters > Transform Background from FontLab's Scripts menu.

Read installation and working with scripts before use.

docs.title: Use Layer As Master
docs.text:
Make a backup or alternate layer the master layer of its glyph.

What it does: Swap the roles of the shown layer and the master layer it belongs to. The shown layer becomes the master layer. The old master layer is kept as "@ HH:MM:SS, DD/MM/YY". Backgrounds (mask layers) travel with their layers: the background of the chosen layer becomes the master background.

How it works: FontLab decides by layer name which layer is the master layer of a master (see "Display Next Layer"). So the script only renames. It renames the old master layer to the backup name, then the chosen layer to the master name, and renames their mask layers to match the FontLab mask-name rule ("mask.", or plain "mask" for the layer of a single-master font). Shapes, anchors, guides and metrics stay in the layer objects. Nothing is cloned, so nothing is lost. One notification covers all layers: one Undo step.

Why this design: - Renaming keeps every property of both layers. The Glyphs original must copy paths, components, anchors and sidebearing keys one by one. - Names are simulated before the first rename. A clash stops the run early. - If a rename fails, the script puts the old names back. - Locked, mask, service, automatic and image layers are refused. So is a glyph that has an automatic layer, or is a base of one (also through manual composites): FontLab cannot undo it. Queued ids and their possible date changes are disclosed. The shared module fly.ap.core.history.glyphs does these checks and the one-step write.

How to use: Show a backup layer (see "Display Next Layer"). Run the script. Check compatibility with the other masters afterwards: a swapped layer can have a different point structure.

Benefit: Restore an earlier state of a master in one step and keep the current one.

Credit: Behaviour after Pedro Arilla's Glyphs script "Use layer as master" (Apache-2.0). Independent rewrite. No source code was copied.

Run Masters > Use Layer As Master from FontLab's Scripts menu.

Read installation and working with scripts before use.

docs.title: Alignment Zones
docs.text:
Edit the alignment zones of every master in one table; Apply is one Undo step.

What it does: Opens a non-modal panel for the current font. Pick a master to list its top and bottom zones. Add a top or bottom zone, remove the selected rows, or edit the position, width and name. "Suggest from o / O" replaces the chosen master's zones with zones from the overshoots of o and O at the baseline, x-height and cap height. Edits stay staged for each master until Apply. Apply writes every changed master as one Undo step; the current master does not change. A top zone covers the area above its position, a bottom zone the area below.

How it works: The panel and its zone model are shared with the App. The native backend reads each master's zones and metrics, then puts the current master back. Apply checks that the font, its masters and its zones are still as read, then writes each changed master as FontLab's Font Info does and reads all masters back.

Why this design: One shared panel and one zone writer keep the staging rules, the refusals and the Undo step the same for every tool that edits zones.

How to use: Open a font, activate its Font window and run Metrics > Alignment Zones. Edit the zones of each master, then press Apply. Use Edit > Undo in the Font window to revert the whole Apply. Reopen the panel after you switch fonts.

Benefit: Stage the zones of a whole family together and apply them in one step.

Limitations: - Every zone needs a name, unique within its master's top or bottom list. Added rows get FontLab's names, such as "T: 500" or "B: 0". Apply refuses an empty or repeated name, and a zero-width row that FontLab would read as the other kind; the panel stays open so that you can fix the row. - A cell that is not a number rejects the whole table; no row is dropped. - Apply needs the Font window of this font as the active window. It refuses while a Glyph window is the active canvas. - Apply re-creates every zone guide of a changed master: the guides get new ids, x-centre 0 and the font guideline style. Only position, width, name, tags and lock stay. A failed Apply that restores the zones also re-creates the guides. Font Info does the same. - FontLab defect fl#8574: after Edit > Undo or Redo, the metric guides show 3 of 9 lines until you reopen the font. The saved file is correct. - The panel does not refresh FontLab's other windows with UpdateAll.

Credit: Adapted from metrics_zones_editor.py, the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. Its table and staging live in the shared App panel.

Run Metrics > Alignment Zones from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Centre In Advance
docs.text:
Centre the outline of each selected glyph in its advance width.

What it does: moves the outline so that both sidebearings are equal. You can also give the glyph a new advance width at the same time: keep it, set it, or change it by an amount.

How it works: the white space is the new width minus the width of the ink. The left sidebearing is half of it, in whole units. The right sidebearing takes the odd unit. Anchors move with the outline. A glyph without outline is listed and skipped. A negative new width is refused for that layer.

Why: symbols, figures, spaces with marks and accents must sit in the middle of their box. Doing it by hand is slow and error prone.

How to use: select glyphs in the Font window. Choose the width mode and the value. Choose the current master or all masters. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection again.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). This includes a base that reaches an auto glyph through other composites. Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own maths, its planner and its controls.

Benefit: exact centring in all masters in one step.

Credit: adapted from the author's own rescued FontLab sample metrics_center_in_advance.py (Apache-2.0).

Run Metrics > Centre In Advance from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Copy Metrics From Reference
docs.text:
Give the selected glyphs the sidebearings or the advance width of a reference glyph.

What it does: copies the metrics of one reference glyph to the selected glyphs, on the current master or on all masters. Four modes are available: "LSB and RSB", "LSB only", "RSB only" and "Advance width (centred)". An optional offset is added to each copied value.

How it works: each master takes the reference values of the same master, so a multi-master family keeps its progression. Sidebearings are read from the outline edges in whole units. In the sidebearing modes the outline moves in place by the LSB change (anchors move with it) and the advance width becomes LSB + outline width + RSB. In "Advance width (centred)" the advance becomes the reference advance plus the offset; the change is shared by both sides, and the right side takes the odd unit. The reference glyph itself is never edited. A master without a reference layer, a reference without outline (sidebearing modes) and a layer without outline are listed and skipped. A result with a negative width is refused for that layer.

Why: related glyphs share their spacing: n, m, h and u take the sidebearings of n; H, I and N take those of H; figures take one tabular width. Copying values by hand in every master is slow and error prone.

How to use: select the glyphs to change in the Font window. Type the reference glyph name; the completer lists the glyphs of the font. Choose the mode, the offset and the current master or all masters. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection and the glyph list again.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own maths, its planner and its controls.

Benefit: consistent spacing groups in all masters in one step, with a preview.

Credit: adapted from metrics_copy_from_reference.py, the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0.

docs.title: Equalize Sidebearings
docs.text:
Make the left and right sidebearings of each selected glyph equal.

What it does: gives both sidebearings the same value, on the current master or on all masters. Five rules are available. "Average of both" keeps the advance width and splits the white space. "Both = LSB", "Both = RSB", "Both = the smaller" and "Both = the larger" copy one value to the other side, so the advance width changes.

How it works: the sidebearings are read from the outline edges in whole units. For "Average of both", the left side gets half of the white space, rounded down; the right side takes the odd unit. The outline moves in place (anchors move with it) and the advance gets the new width. A layer without outline is listed and skipped. A rule that gives a negative width is refused for that layer.

Why: symmetric letters such as O, H, o and n, and many symbols, start with equal sidebearings. Setting both sides by hand in each master is slow and error prone.

How to use: select glyphs in the Font window. Choose the rule. Choose the current master or all masters. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection again.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own rules, its planner and its controls.

Benefit: symmetric spacing in all masters in one step, with a preview.

Credit: adapted from metrics_equalize_sidebearings.py, the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0.

docs.title: Italic Sidebearings
docs.text:
Report and set sidebearings along the italic angle.

What it does: shows two pairs of sidebearings for each layer. The plain pair is the distance from the advance edge to the ink, measured sideways. The italic pair is measured after the outline is de-slanted by the italic angle. You can add to the italic values or set them.

How it works: the script maps the outline through a shear around the height "measured at" (half of the x-height by default). The sheared outline gives the italic edges. A change moves the real outline sideways and changes the advance. Anchors move with the outline. All values are whole units.

Why: in a slanted design the plain sidebearings depend on the overhang of the slant. The italic sidebearings let you compare and space an italic "n" and "o" as if they were upright.

How to use: select glyphs in the Font window. Check the angle and the height. Choose "Add" or "Set". Tick LSB and RSB and enter the values. Choose the current master or all masters. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection again.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). This includes a base that reaches an auto glyph through other composites. Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own maths, its planner and its controls.

Benefit: you space italics with the same method as upright designs.

Credit: adapted from the author's own rescued FontLab sample metrics_italic_sidebearings.py (Apache-2.0).

Run Metrics > Italic Sidebearings from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Round Advances
docs.text:
Round advance widths to a step. Outlines stay where they are.

What it does: rounds the advance width of each target glyph to a multiple of the step (2 to 100 units). Choose the nearest multiple, the next one up, or the next one down. A half step goes up for "nearest".

How it works: the right sidebearing takes the whole change. The left sidebearing, the outline and the anchors do not move. The table lists only the layers that change. Each Apply plans again from the live font.

Why: interpolation and scaling leave fractional or odd advances. A rounded advance keeps the spacing on a clean grid. The left edge that you already set stays fixed.

How to use: select glyphs in the Font window, or choose all glyphs. Choose the current master or all masters. Set the step. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection again.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). This includes a base that reaches an auto glyph through other composites. Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own maths, its planner and its controls.

docs.title: Scale Advances
docs.text:
Scale advance widths by a percentage. Each outline stays centred.

What it does: multiplies the advance width of each selected glyph by a percentage (10 to 400 percent). The new width is a whole number of units.

How it works: the change in width is split between both sidebearings. The outline moves by half of the change. The right sidebearing takes the odd unit. Anchors move with the outline. The table lists the old width, the new width and the shift for each layer.

Why: loosening a Bold master or tightening a Display master is a common job. Splitting the change keeps the balance of every glyph. A plain scale of the advance alone would push the ink to one side.

How to use: select glyphs in the Font window. Choose the current master or all masters. Enter the percentage. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection again.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). This includes a base that reaches an auto glyph through other composites. Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own maths, its planner and its controls.

Benefit: open or tighten the spacing of many glyphs in one step. The balance of each glyph is kept.

docs.title: Sidebearing Offset Preview
docs.text:
Preview how a sidebearing offset would shift the selected glyphs.

What: Opens a modeless panel with offset controls: a minimum, a maximum and a value, plus a choice of horizontal or vertical orientation and two invert options for the control itself. For every selected glyph layer the report shows what the geometric sidebearings would become if the ink moved by the chosen offset: the left sidebearing grows by the offset, the right shrinks by it and the advance width stays the same. Values are whole font units from -100 to 100.

Use: Select glyphs in a Font window, or glyph layers in a Glyph window. Run Metrics > Sidebearing Offset Preview. Move the offset control and read the report. Press Refresh Selection after you change the selection, the master or the outlines. Close the panel when you are done. With nothing selected the report asks you to refresh after selecting glyph layers.

Safety: Read-only preview. The panel says that font data is unchanged, and it is. The tool reads the selected layers, their advances and their ink extent. It writes no font data, metrics, selection, history, preference, clipboard or Output text. Nothing is applied; use the Metrics editors to set sidebearings. If the font or selection changes while the tool reads it, it refuses to publish a partial result.

Source: Original workflow built on the shared App spacing offset preview (fly.ap.metrics.offset.model), Apache-2.0. Requires App>=1.2.0 and fontlab-fly in FontLab 9 Python 3.11.

Run Metrics > Sidebearing Offset Preview from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Sidebearings Tuner
docs.text:
Set, add to or scale the sidebearings of the selected glyphs.

What it does: changes the left sidebearing (LSB), the right sidebearing (RSB) or both, on the current master or on all masters. "Add" adds a value to each side; a negative value tightens. "Set to" gives each side a value. "Scale %" multiplies each side by a percentage.

How it works: the sidebearings are read from the outline edges in whole units. The new value of each ticked side is computed in whole units; a half unit rounds up. An unticked side keeps its value. The outline moves in place by the LSB change (anchors move with it) and the advance width becomes LSB + outline width + RSB. A layer without outline is listed and skipped. A change that gives a negative width is refused for that layer.

Why: spacing passes often need the same correction on many glyphs and in every master, for example "+5 on both sides" or "RSB 40 on all round letters".

How to use: select glyphs in the Font window. Choose the operation. Tick the sides to change and type their values. Choose the current master or all masters. Check the table. Press Apply. The panel stays open. Press "Use selection" to read the Font window selection again. The panel opens on "Add" with 0, so the first preview changes nothing. Switching to "Scale %" turns a value of 0 into 100 %, which also changes nothing; leaving "Scale %" turns only that untouched 100 back into 0. A value that you typed is kept.

Safety: each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto glyphs is refused, because FontLab rebuilds the auto glyphs and may lose their anchors and locks (FontLab issue 8512). Tick "Edit bases of auto glyphs anyway" to go on. Apply discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. After the write the script reads advance and outline back and reports any mismatch. A failure after the write started says so and asks you to use Edit > Undo. It does not call UpdateAll (FontLab issue 8537).

Shared parts: the panel, the plan model, the one-step write and the read-back come from the App module fly.ap.metrics.panel.model. This script holds its own maths, its planner and its controls.

Benefit: exact sidebearing corrections on many glyphs and masters in one step, with a preview.

Credit: adapted from metrics_sidebearings_tuner.py, the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0.

docs.title: Spacing String Preview
docs.text:
Render a spacing control string such as HOHnono from the font's own outlines and advances.

What it does: Type characters or /glyphname tokens, pick a master, and judge the rhythm of straight and round sidebearings without generating a font. Advance boxes and LSB/RSB numbers can be shown under each glyph. Nothing is edited; the preview follows the outlines as they are now.

How it works: Resolve text tokens to current outline paths and advances on the chosen master. Draw optional advance boxes and sidebearing values below each glyph.

Why this design: Control strings isolate spacing rhythm; the preview uses the font drawings directly and does not add kerning to hide raw spacing.

How to use: Run Metrics > Spacing String Preview. Enter a control string, choose a master and enable boxes or numbers as needed. Compare straight and round glyphs at the chosen size.

Benefit: Judge current spacing without generating a font or changing advance widths.

Run Metrics > Spacing String Preview from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: TMetrics Window
docs.text:
Set text in the current font and adjust its spacing and kerning.

What: Opens a modeless TMetrics window on the current font. Type text, or /glyphnames, and choose features, direction, script and language. The canvas shows the set rows with the baseline, the vertical metric lines, glyph boxes, sidebearing marks and kerning. The readout gives the selected glyph's advance, left and right sidebearings and the kerning pair before it. With App's fontui-shaping extra (uharfbuzz) the text is shaped; without it characters map to glyphs one to one and the window says the text is unshaped. Edits you make in FontLab, and Undo or Redo, appear in the window shortly after.

Use: Open a font and run Metrics > TMetrics Window. Type text in the field. Click a glyph, or press Left, Right, Home or End, to select it. Type a value in the LSB, RSB, Width or Kerning field and press Return. Alt+Left or Alt+Right nudges the right sidebearing by 1 unit, and Ctrl+Alt+Left or Ctrl+Alt+Right nudges the kerning of the pair before the selected glyph; add Shift for steps of 10. Double-click a glyph to open it in a TGlyph window.

Safety: The window writes only the values you change: the selected glyph's sidebearings or width on the default layer, and the kerning of the pair before it. Each write is one named undo step; each auto-repeated nudge is a separate step. It writes no preferences or clipboard. It prints a message to Output only when App or Fly is missing. Round-trip with a live FontLab font is not yet verified natively; try it on a copy first.

Source: Original workflow built on the shared App TMetrics window (fly.ap.fontui.tmetrics), Apache-2.0. Requires a FontLabApp build providing fontlabapp.fontui.tmetrics, with its fontport extra and fontlab-fly in FontLab 9 Python 3.11.

Run Metrics > TMetrics Window from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Vertical Metrics Diagram
docs.text:
Compare the vertical metrics of every master with real outlines, side by side.

What it does: shows one column per master. Each column draws the outlines of H, x, b and p from that master against its baseline, ascender, cap height, x-height and descender lines. A cap height that misses the H, or an x-height that cuts the x, shows at a glance. The panel only reads the font; it never changes it.

How it works: the metric values come from FontMetrics(package, master) for each master, the same reader as Masters > Overview, so the current master is never switched. The outlines are read in place from each layer's contours, with component transforms applied, into one QPainterPath per glyph. One scale fits the tallest and the lowest metric of all masters and the widest sample line, so the columns compare directly. Line names stand in the left margin. A sample glyph that the font lacks, or that has no layer in a master, is listed below the diagram and left out; it never stops the panel. Drawing errors are kept in the panel and the painter always ends.

Why: wrong vertical metrics are easy to miss in a table of numbers and costly to find late, in proofs or after export. A picture of all masters with their own outlines makes the error visible before it spreads.

How to use: open a font and run the script. The panel stays open. Press Reload after you change the metrics or the sample glyphs. To change the values, use Font Info > Master Metrics Table (or FontLab's Font Info); this diagram does not edit.

Benefit: a quick visual check of ascender, cap height, x-height and descender against real letters in every master, without a risk to the font.

Credit: adapted from metrics_vertical_metrics_diagram.py, the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. The editing part of that sample is left to Font Info > Master Metrics Table.

Run Metrics > Vertical Metrics Diagram from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Width Table
docs.text:
Advance widths of the selected glyphs across all masters, sortable, with odd progressions flagged.

What it does: In a weight family the widths usually grow (or shrink) steadily from master to master. A glyph whose width goes up and then down again is flagged: often a spacing slip. Click a column header to sort; "Select flagged" selects those glyphs in the Font window. Nothing is edited.

How it works: Read selected glyph advances in master order and classify their progression. Show numeric master columns and flag mixed increasing/decreasing sequences.

Why this design: A mixed progression is a spacing-review candidate, not proof that the design is wrong; selection leaves the decision to the user.

How to use: Select glyphs and run Metrics > Width Table. Sort columns or restrict the view to mixed progressions, then use Select flagged to locate the reported glyphs.

Benefit: Find unusual master width trends without changing advances or outlines.

docs.title: Zero-Width Marks
docs.text:
Set the advance width of combining marks to zero.

What it does: gives each selected combining mark an advance width of 0. A combining mark is a glyph with a Unicode category of Mn or Me, or a name that ends in "comb". Other glyphs are ignored unless you clear the filter.

How it works: you choose where the outline goes. "Keep" leaves the outline in place. "Hang left" moves it left by the old width, so it sits over the preceding glyph. "Centre" puts the middle of the ink on x = 0. Anchors move with the outline.

docs.title: Batch Glyph Notes
docs.text:
Set or append one note on every selected glyph at once.

WHAT: A non-modal panel takes a note text and an operation. Set replaces each glyph note (an empty Set clears the notes). Append adds the text on a new line after the existing note. A table shows every note before and after. Apply writes only the glyphs whose note changes.

HOW: The script reads the selection through the shared App selection reader and scans the whole font. For the write it rescans, plans, and writes as one Undo step: layers and glyph in one notify list (a glyph alone adds no Undo step). After the write it reads each note back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fly.ap.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo.

WHY: A glyph note belongs to the glyph, not to a master. FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer is notified, and Undo does not restore them. So the script REFUSES glyphs that own an auto layer, shows the reason in the table, and never puts an auto layer in the notify list. A base glyph of an auto composite may get a note (native check pending). The script never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph (that getter can clear a fresh note mirror on build 9784), never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537), and discloses queued ids and their possible date changes.

USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose Set or Append, type the note, check the table, press Apply. Press Reload selection after you change the selection.

BENEFIT: Review comments or to-do remarks reach many glyphs in one undoable step, with a preview.

Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

Run Names > Batch Glyph Notes from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Batch Rename
docs.text:
Find and replace in glyph names, with a live preview and strict checks.

WHAT: A non-modal panel takes a Find text (plain or regular expression) and a Replace text. It lists every glyph whose name would change, with the new name and a check result. Rename applies all rows that pass.

HOW: The script scans the font on open and on Reload, and again before the write. A row passes only when the new name is valid, does not exist, is not the target of another row, and the glyph is not tied to an auto layer. The write is one Undo step. The rename uses the font-owned FontGate record, never flGlyph.fgGlyph. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fly.ap.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo.

WHY: FontLab would replace an existing glyph that has the new name, so the script refuses that. FontLab rebuilds auto layers when they are notified (it turned ecircumflex into a lone "ee" after e was renamed). So the script REFUSES glyphs that have auto layers and glyphs that are the base of an auto composite, also through other composites. It never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537) and refuses to hide queued ids; it discloses their possible date changes. Kerning and features keep the old names.

USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Type Find and Replace. Use \1 for groups in regular-expression mode. Press Rename. Choose "All glyphs" to rename across the font.

BENEFIT: Bulk renames (for example uniXXXX to AGL names) are safe, previewed and reversible with one Edit > Undo.

Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

Run Names > Batch Rename from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Case Pairs
docs.text:
Find the upper- or lowercase counterparts of the selected glyphs and select them.

What it does: Counterparts come from Unicode case mapping of each glyph's code point; unencoded alternates use their base name (a.ss01 -> A.ss01). Select the counterparts alone or together with the originals. Nothing in the font changes.

How it works: Map Unicode case counterparts to existing glyphs. For unencoded suffixed names, try the base counterpart with the original suffix; reject multi- character case expansions.

Why this design: A Unicode case change is not always one glyph, so missing or expanding mappings remain visible rather than guessed.

How to use: Select source glyphs and run Names > Case Pairs. Review the mapping rows, choose whether originals stay selected and select the available counterparts.

Benefit: Move between related case glyphs while preserving names, encodings and outlines.

docs.title: Character Info
docs.text:
A live panel describing the character of the glyph selected in the Font window.

What it does: Shows the outline next to the system font's rendering, the code point, the Unicode name and category (Python's unicodedata), case counterpart, decomposition and the UTF-8/UTF-16 encodings. It follows the selection twice a second; nothing in the font changes.

How it works: Describe the selected glyph's encoded character with Python Unicode data. Draw its current outline beside a system-font character and refresh from the live selection.

Why this design: The separate renderings distinguish character identity from the font's own drawing without treating the system glyph as a design target.

How to use: Run Names > Character Info. Select an encoded glyph in the Font window, inspect its code point and encodings and use Copy to copy the current character.

Benefit: Check Unicode identity, case and decomposition while leaving the glyph's encoding unchanged.

docs.title: Glyph Notes
docs.text:
Read and edit the note of one glyph. Browse every glyph that has a note.

WHAT: A non-modal panel shows the note of the first glyph selected in the Font window in an editor. Save writes it. A list below shows all glyphs that have a note. A click loads that note into the editor. A double-click also selects the glyph in the Font window.

HOW: The script scans the whole font. Save rescans, then writes one note as one Undo step: layers and glyph in one notify list (a glyph alone adds no Undo step). It then reads the note back and compares it with the text. Double-click selection goes through the App selection helper, which checks that a regular Font window is active (fl#8528). The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fly.ap.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo.

WHY: FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer is notified, and Undo does not restore them. So the script REFUSES to save a note on a glyph that owns an auto layer, says why, and never puts an auto layer in the notify list. A base glyph of an auto composite may get a note (native check pending). The script never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph (that getter can clear a fresh note mirror on build 9784), never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537), and discloses queued ids and their possible date changes.

USE: Select a glyph in the Font window. Run the script. Edit the note. Press Save note. Pick a row in the list to edit another glyph.

BENEFIT: Notes travel with the glyph in .vfc and .vfj files. The list gives an overview of all remarks in the font. One Edit > Undo reverts one save.

Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

What: Link whole-word Bold, Italic and Oblique styles to an available base. Width groups remain separate. ExtraBold and SemiBold are not Bold. Close releases owned signals. Benefit: Preview regular/bold/italic relationships across the complete family. docs.title: Suffix Tool
docs.text:
Add, remove or replace a glyph-name suffix (.ss01, .sc, .alt) on the selected glyphs.

WHAT: A non-modal panel offers three operations. Add puts a suffix on each selected name. Remove strips one suffix (or the last suffix when the field is empty). Replace swaps one suffix for another. A table previews every new name and a check result. Apply renames all rows that pass.

HOW: The script rescans the font before the write. A row passes only when the new name is valid, does not exist, is not the target of another row, and the glyph is not tied to an auto layer. The write is one Undo step. The rename and the optional Unicode removal use the font-owned FontGate record, never flGlyph.fgGlyph. After clearing Unicode the script reads the list back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fly.ap.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo.

WHY: Suffixed alternates are normally unencoded, so the panel can clear their Unicode in the same step. FontLab would replace an existing glyph that has the new name, so the script refuses that. FontLab rebuilds auto layers when they are notified, so the script REFUSES glyphs that have auto layers and glyphs that are the base of an auto composite, also through other composites. It never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537) and discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. Before it removes Unicode, the script applies the guards of the App Unicode writer: a regular Font window must be active and no Glyph editor may be open.

USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the operation, type or pick a suffix (a missing leading dot is added), then press Apply.

BENEFIT: Alternate sets (.ss01, .sc, .case) get consistent names in one previewed, undoable step.

docs.title: Unicode From Names
docs.text:
Assign Unicode code points that the glyph names imply. Preview first.

WHAT: A non-modal panel reads glyph names and lists the code point each name implies. It knows uniXXXX and uXXXX[XX] names, a built-in table of Adobe Glyph List names, and accented Latin names (Wacute is LATIN CAPITAL LETTER W WITH ACUTE, found with unicodedata). Names with a suffix (a.ss01), ligature names (f_i) and surrogate code points (U+D800 to U+DFFF) are left alone. Assign writes all rows marked "assign".

HOW: The script scans the font and plans each row: "same" (already right), "encoded differently" (the glyph has another code and Replace is off), "used by X" (another glyph already owns the code, or an earlier row claims it), a refusal reason, or "assign". The write rescans, then sets the code points on the font-owned FontGate record as one Undo step. It reads each list back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fly.ap.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo.

WHY: A code point must belong to one glyph only. The plan never steals a code from another glyph and never lets two rows claim one code. FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer, or the base glyph of an auto composite (also through other composites), is notified, and Undo does not restore them. So the script REFUSES such glyphs. It never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph, never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537), discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. Before it writes, the script applies the guards of the App Unicode writer: a regular Font window must be active and no Glyph editor may be open.

USE: Select glyphs in the Font window, or choose "All glyphs in the font". Run the script. Check the table. Press Assign.

BENEFIT: Fonts built from named outlines get a correct character map in one previewed, undoable step.
