docs.title: Glyphs Between Oldstyle Figures
docs.text:
Open a new native Glyph tab with glyphs between oldstyle figures.

Select glyphs in a Font window or occurrences in a Glyph window, then run this Proof command. Keep their actual order and repeated editor occurrences. The new tab uses the font's current master; source layer overrides are not copied. The selected glyph name appears between each context name, or inside repeated H, I, HHOHH or nnonn contexts, as indicated by the command. Between sequences end with the selected glyph and two newlines per occurrence. Surround sequences end with one final context. With no selection, Between opens an empty tab; Surround opens its context alone. The original behavior is retained.

App builds all glyph-name rows before opening. Named native symbols retain unencoded glyphs and oldstyle .osf names without slash-text or Unicode fallback. No context is filtered or substituted when a name is missing. One deadline covers selected-layer capture, generation, symbols and preflight. A changed source selection/font or invalid input refuses the complete operation. A named-content writer can target only a verified new active tab belonging to the captured source font. It never populates an existing or foreign tab. Native failure can leave a new tab; no atomic UI rollback is claimed. The owned native sender is disconnected and deleted.

This adaptation preserves Output instead of clearing/printing status. It calls no glyph geometry, history, preference or master writer. Requires App>=1.2.0 and Fly in FontLab9 Python3.11. Adapted from Pedro Arilla's Apache-2.0 Glyphs between/Glyphs between figures_old.py. See NOTICE and additional-tools.json for complete source/license provenance.

Run Proof > Glyphs Between Oldstyle Figures from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Highest & Lowest Glyphs
docs.text:
Open the exact highest and lowest foreground layers in a fresh FontLab tab.

Run this Proof command with a font open. Scan all foreground masters and ordinary auxiliary layers; omit masks/service caches. Keep font glyph order and the first layer on equal coordinates. Empty bounds participate, and the same winner appears twice when it is both extrema. Preserve unencoded glyph names and exact layer names rather than substituting Unicode or slash text. Missing/ambiguous layers and stale/slow reads fail before a proof. A modeless coordinate panel preserves the source messages without changing Output. Run Again repeats the complete scan and new-tab action.

Fly loads shared App capture, extrema selection and native named-layer tabs. No missing layer is created; no master/selection/font/history/Output writer or application-wide event loop is used. A native tab failure can leave a new tab; no atomic UI rollback is claimed. Requires App>=1.2.0 and Fly in FontLab9/Python3.11. Modified from slobzheninov--Glyphs-Scripts/Testing/Highest & Lowest Glyphs.py; see NOTICE/additional-tools.json. The port fixes zero being mistaken for an unset extrema value.

docs.title: Hoefler Lowercase
docs.text:
Open the complete Hoefler Lowercase kerning proof in 1 new FontLab Glyph tab(s).

Open a font and run this Proof command. Use the native nonmodal Glyph editor to inspect spacing and kerning. Existing tabs remain. KernKing creates lowercase first, then mixed case; the other commands create one tab. Every original word, Unicode character, repeated space, slash-name escape and blank line is retained. No missing character is filtered or replaced by this script. Native /quoteright and /germandbls names stay names; doubled slash requests a literal slash.

Fly loads the shared App implementation. Complete resources load before native work. Font and current master are captured once and checked before each tab. A switched source or expired preflight refuses; later-tab failure can leave an earlier new tab. The native creation call is not preemptible and UI rollback is not claimed. Shared ownership disconnects/deletes senders and restores original shape activation. No font geometry, kerning, history, preference or Output writer is called. The source's undefined Font global is repaired by explicit lookup; its Output clearing/printing is omitted to preserve the user's existing Output.

Requires App>=1.2.0 and Fly with FontLab Python3.11. Adapted from Pedro Arilla's Apache-2.0 Kerning/Hoefler Lowercase.py. Complete original and proof-text credits, resource hashes and licence are in NOTICE/additional-tools.json.

Run Proof > Hoefler Lowercase from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Random Lowercase Nontext
docs.text:
Open a new FontLab Glyph tab with random lowercase nontext.

Open a font and run this Proof command. It uses the current font and opens one new tab, preserving existing tabs. Run again to get another proof. Content is 700 lowercase letters; draw a divisor from 3, 5 and 7 at every index. Keep all source draw order, spaces, duplicate entries and compound names. Spaces for non-text/numbers follow index modulo a fresh random divisor, including index zero. Words keep their final space. Do not trim or filter characters absent from the font; send them unchanged to the native editor.

Shared App code generates the complete text before a tab is opened. Fly loads App. The native doCreateTextBlock operation opens the new FontLab Glyph tab. No application-wide event loop or replacement editor is needed. No open font is an error before random draws/tab creation. Resource/generation failure opens no tab. A native tab failure propagates; it may leave an empty new tab, so atomic rollback is not claimed. Native tab content, missing-character handling, source-font binding and full data/history preservation remain pending.

The port repairs the source's undefined Font global with explicit current-font lookup. It preserves Output instead of clearing it or printing status there. Requires App>=1.2.0 and Fly in FontLab9 Python3.11. Adapted from Pedro Arilla's Apache-2.0 Random/Random lowercase non-text.py. See NOTICE and additional-tools.json for source/data/license provenance.

Run Proof > Random Lowercase Nontext from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Case Coverage
docs.text:
Find missing uppercase and lowercase counterparts and export-policy conflicts.

What it does: Check the current font or every open font. Report missing uppercase and lowercase counterparts, alternate encoded names and export-policy conflicts. Open an ordered proof of each problem, reusing the current proof when asked.

How it works: Read detached FontGate names and alternative encodings. Glyport supplies maintained GlyphData categories. The caller supplies canonical GlyphData names to App's host-free engine. Canonical names win; the first encoded alias in font order follows, and all ambiguous aliases remain in the report. Multi-character case mappings stay complete; i_dotaccentcomb maps to i and SS maps to Germandbls. Other expansions use complete GlyphData component names joined by underscores; unknown component mappings stay unknown. Math exclusions and ligatures remain visible in detailed diagnostics. The public.skipExportGlyphs compatibility policy defines export status; this is not a guarantee about FontLab's binary exporter.

Why this design: Preserve mekkablue's Casefolding Report controls and source-order proofs while correcting its ord() failure on multi-character case mappings. Shared App mechanics own capture, proofs, settings and window lifetime.

How to use: Open a font and run Reports > Case Coverage. Choose the four controls and click Report. Use Show detailed report to read the complete per-font rows. Exclude math symbols suppresses missing counterparts only. Reuse current tab controls proof placement. When inactive views are ambiguous, choose the exact existing view and click Report again. FontLab does not expose Glyphs' remembered-tab order. The exact text-block binding is checked at runtime; unsupported bindings refuse proof creation/replacement with guidance. Installed native proof usability remains unqualified. Open detailed report window shows diagnostics automatically; it never clears or writes FontLab's Output panel. Refresh font availability after opening a font. Close the panel when done.

Benefit: Find incomplete case pairs and compatibility export mismatches before proofing.

Credits: Workflow: mekkablue/Glyphs-Scripts/Glyph Names, Notes and Unicode/ Casefolding Report.py, Apache-2.0. Reimplementation; no source body copied.

Run Reports > Case Coverage from FontLab's Scripts menu.

docs.title: Close But No Cigar
docs.text:
Report nearly correct angles, stem lengths and node positions in every selected glyph's first layer.

Select glyphs in a Font or Glyph window, then run this script. The modeless, read-only report offers selectable text, Refresh and Close. It uses the first layer in each selected parent, not the selected or active layer, and that layer's associated named master's PostScript stems and ascender, cap height, x height and descender. Every own contour and node, including handles, is checked.

Original strict boundaries and exact-value exclusions remain: angles within 2 degrees of 0/180/+90/-90, stem lengths within 5%, and coordinates within 2 units of zero or the four metrics. Exact match to any stem suppresses all near matches for that orientation. Duplicate targets and selected occurrences remain ordered. Components are omitted; own shape transforms are applied.

Simon Cozens' glyphmonkey wraps last-to-first even for open paths; this report retains that edge and its 50-step cubic-length sampling (last sample below 1). It repairs the cubic angle method/property bug. Empty contours are safe. Quadratic/malformed segments, generated/projective shapes, unknown associated masters and unreadable or changed sources refuse the entire report. Refresh clears failed results. No Output, font, selection, history, preference, clipboard or file writer runs. Native getter preservation and lifetime remain pending. Requires FontLab 9 Python 3.11, Fly and App 1.2.0 or later. docs.title: Event Log
docs.text:
Print what happens in FontLab to the Output panel: font, window, glyph, layer, selection and edits.

What it does: While its small panel is open, every switch of the active font, window or tab, glyph, master or layer, and every change of glyph or node selection is printed as one line in the Output panel. Undo and redo, saving, opening and closing fonts, tool changes, kerning, features, metrics and font info edits are printed too. Nothing in the font changes.

How it works: The panel listens to FontLab's own notifications. Switching notifications arrive in bursts, so they are gathered for a moment, then the current state is read once and only the parts that changed are printed. Other notifications are printed as they come, without repeats within the same second.

Why this design: Notifications cost nothing while nothing happens, so the log stays lightweight. Comparing states instead of trusting each notification keeps the log short and correct when FontLab sends several at once.

How to use: Run Reports > Event Log, open the Output panel and work as usual. Close the panel to stop logging.

Benefit: See exactly which font, glyph and layer a script or tool will act on, and which actions FontLab reports, while you work.

docs.title: Nodes Near Zones
docs.text:
Find on-curve nodes that sit within a few units of a vertical metric but not on it.

What it does: Near misses (y = 687 when the cap height is 688) are almost always slips of the mouse; real overshoots are further away and pass. Checks baseline, x-height, cap height, ascender and descender of every master. Select the glyphs to fix them. Nothing in the font changes.

How it works: Transform own on-curve node positions into layer coordinates. Report points with a nonzero distance within the chosen tolerance of each master's vertical metrics.

Why this design: A near-miss report is a review aid; small offsets can be intentional and must not be snapped automatically.

How to use: Run Reports > Nodes Near Zones. Choose selection or whole font and a tolerance, inspect glyph/master/metric rows and select results to examine them in FontLab.

Benefit: Find nodes close to metric lines without moving nodes, handles, components or anchors.

docs.title: Smallcap Consistency
docs.text:

What it does: Count exporting upper, lower and smallcap glyphs. List missing .sc/.smcp and .sc/.c2sc counterparts, orphan smallcaps, missing capitals/lowercase and left/right smallcap-to-capital kerning-group differences.

How it works: Capture detached metadata from the current font and master. Use Unicode case mappings with alternate suffixes intact, including ligatures and multi-character mappings. docs.title: Find Font Files
docs.text:
Search the files of one folder for a piece of text, such as a glyph name.

What: Opens a modeless search window with three fields: Named (a file name pattern), Containing text and In directory (it starts in your Documents folder). The window searches the files directly inside that folder (it does not descend into sub-folders) and lists every file that contains the text, with the table filling in while the search runs. Use it to find which font sources, feature files or scripts mention a glyph name, a feature tag or a family name.

Use: Run Utilities > Find Font Files. Press Browse to pick a folder, type the text, press Find and watch the result table. Double-click a result, or press Return on it, to open that file with the application your system has for it. Press Cancel to stop a search that is still running. Closing the window also stops it and releases the files it had opened.

Safety: Only reads files. The search opens files in the chosen folder for reading and never changes, moves, creates or deletes a file. It does not read or write font data, selection, history, preferences, clipboard or Output text, and it never imports or runs the files it searches. Opening a result is an explicit double-click and is handed to the normal desktop opener, which may start another application.

Source: Original workflow built on the shared App file finder (fly.ap.qt.find_files.model), Apache-2.0. Requires App>=1.2.0 and fontlab-fly in FontLab 9 Python 3.11.

docs.title: Magic Remover
docs.text:
Remove corresponding selected items from compatible glyph layers.

What: Preview selected polygon nodes, whole contours and components on every compatible foreground master or intermediate layer of one glyph. If any compatible master must keep an item, every master keeps that item. How: Match stored shape, contour and node indices and component bases. Use the shared outline writer. Components retain their original history objects. The change is recorded as one Undo step. Why: FontLab Delete with Preferences > Variations > Synchronize "Remove node" and matching edits removes corresponding nodes, including curve nodes, on the other masters. This panel adds a per-layer preview and explicit kept reasons. Use: Select items in one Glyph window slot. Run the tool, inspect the rows, then press Remove. Use selection refreshes the current editor selection. Benefit: Remove the same detail over compatible masters without repeated edits.

Partial curve-node selections are kept: use FontLab's Delete as described above. The public contour API does not expose curve-preserving node deletion. Whole curved contours can be removed, along with any outline shape left empty. Anchors are not part of selection removal: the public pin binding exposes no selection member. Existing anchors stay unchanged. Polygon endpoints and the minimum of three closed or two open nodes are kept. Masks, service, locked, shared and transformed outlines are kept. Automatic glyphs and their bases are kept. Glyphs corner-component hints have no FontLab counterpart. For a separate outline backup, use Masters > Copy Outline To Mask before removal; this tool never overwrites a mask on a modifier-key press.

Independent behaviour rewrite after Reza Bohloul, RezaBohloul, Edit/Magic Remover.py; no licence declared. Repository: https://github.com/RezaBohloul/RezaBohloul . No source code copied.

docs.title: Reference Image Viewer
docs.text:
View a reference image beside your font, with zoom and fit controls.

What: Opens a modeless image viewer for the artwork you design from: a specimen scan, a sketch or a photograph of lettering. Open a local image file and zoom in and out, fit it to the window or return to its normal size. The viewer scrolls around the image and keeps the zoom centred. A print command sends the image to a printer at native pixel size.

Use: Run Utilities > Reference Image Viewer. Choose File > Open and pick an image. Zoom with the menu or its shortcuts, or use Fit to window. Choose File > Print only when you want a paper copy. Close the window when you are done.

Safety: The viewer reads the image file you choose and writes nothing to it. It does not read or write font data, selection, history, preferences, clipboard or Output text. Printing happens only when you choose Print and confirm the printer dialog. Qt's print dialog can send the image to a printer or write a PDF to any path you pick there. If printing needs a scratch file, it is created in a private temporary folder owned by the viewer, and the viewer removes that folder when it closes. Open, print and help dialogs are asynchronous and belong to the viewer.
